articleTitle: RFID Antenna Near the Surface of Metal
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Nowadays, RFID (radiofrequency identification) technology is becoming more and more popular. One critical problem is that most passive RFID tag can not be placed on metal objects because metallic surface changes its radiation pattern, input impedance, radiation efficiency and resonant frequency. Through detailed theoretical analysis, relationship between the distance to the metallic surface and the tag' s communication efficiency is deduced. Finite element method (FEM) is used to simulate the dependency of antenna efficiency on the distance of the plate. Experiments have also been carried out to verify the analysis and the simulation results. Finally, a recommended distance of RFID tag placed on metallic surface has been given.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of UWB Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A type of antipodal Vivaldi antenna is designed in this paper, which can be used for pulse radiation in UWB communication. Vivaldi antenna is a special tapered slot antenna with planar structure and is easy to be integrated with transmitting elements and receiving elements to form a compact structure. The antenna designed has good performance in the band 3.1GHZ to 10.6GHZ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, which is assigned to Ultra Wide Band (UWB) wireless communication by FCC. The antenna proposed can radiate or receive UWB pulses with little distortion and a good directivity and a high efficiency.

articleTitle: A Modified Grid Array Antenna Radiating a Circularly Polarized Wave
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a modified grid array antenna whose radiation elements are loops, which are designed to radiate a circularly polarized wave. The array antenna has a low profile, that is, the distance from the loops to the ground plane, H, is extremely small: H = 3.5 mm (= 0.08 wavelength at 7 GHz). Analysis reveals that a modified grid array composed of nine loops has a 2.3% frequency bandwidth for a 3-dB axial ratio criterion, with a maximum gain of approximately 15 dBi.

articleTitle: Research on the Millimeter Wave Power Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Power equalizer is often used to adjust the output power of traveling wave tubes (TWT) or high power solid state amplifiers. Traditionally, a power equalizer is composed of coaxial line with electromagnetic wave absorber or microstrip line with resistance in resonance circuit. However, those structures only adapt to lower millimeter wave. In this paper, a millimeter wave power equalizer is fulfilled by waveguide resonance cavity with electromagnetic wave absorber. The measured results and the simulated results show a very good agreement.

articleTitle: Research and Improvement of LEACH Protocol in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The router protocol LEACH and its feasible improvement in Wireless Sensor Networks are discussed here. The performance was simulated in NS2 and the result of the simulation was analyzed in detail. Considering network load balance, multi-hop, node' s remaining energy and other relative factors, some measures were made to prolong the network lifetime and improve the load balance of LEACH.

articleTitle: Broadband Waveguide-to-Microstrip Antipodal Finline Transition without Additional Resonance Preventer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a design of waveguide- to-microstrip antipodal finline transition, which provides a broadband and low insertion loss performance needless of additional resonance frequency preventer in the model. The suppression of resonance frequency depends on the self-structure of the antipodal finline transition. Meanwhile several factors affecting transition performance are taken into account. The design was verified by experimental results at Ka-band, which has a coincidence with the results of simulation. The compact transition design could decrease the complexity of antipodal finline transition and effect of manufacture error.

articleTitle: A Novel DOA estimation Algorithm Based on Eigen Space
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on the investigation to classical DOA algorithm (MUSIC and improved MUSIC), a novel DOA estimation algorithm is proposed which makes full use of signal subspace and noise subspace characteristics. The algorithm can achieve not only DOA estimation but also information source power estimation. The simulation result reveals that the performance of DOA algorithm is better than that of MUSIC and improved MUSIC. In the conditions of coherent sources and small snapshot as well as low SNR, the algorithm can still present a favorable DOA estimation performance. Besides, the complexity of this algorithm is not high, and it is easy to carry out. So the algorithm is predominant and robust.

articleTitle: New Design Method for a Dual band Waveguide Iris Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we present new design method for a square iris polarizer to be used in dual-band (Ka-band; 20.8 ~ 21.2 GHz, 30.6 ~31 GHz) antenna feeds. To act principles for a square iris polarizer, design concept, design method are proposed and Ka-band polarizer is designed using the commercial software HFSS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">reg</sup> The designed polarizer has less than 30 dB return loss and less than 0.3 dB axial ratio in all operation band.

articleTitle: A New Shaped Reflector Antenna for Wide Beam Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a new shaped reflector antenna for wide beam azimuthal patterns and a cosecant squared elevation pattern. Elliptical strips instead of parabolic strips are used in horizontal planes of the reflector surface to achieve this purpose. Simulation and measurement results of the shaped reflector fed by a ridged horn antenna are presented.

articleTitle: Microwave Holographic Imaging of Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common forms of cancer in women. X-ray mammography is the most widely used technique for early detection but has limitations. In this paper, an alternative approach for breast cancer detection using microwave imaging is presented. This is based upon a microwave holographic approach, central to which is the use of a synthetic reference beam. This approach has benefits in terms of simplicity and expense. Experimental results using a breast phantom are included to demonstrate the potential of this approach.

articleTitle: A Low-Power AC/DC Rectifier for Passive UHF RFID Transponders
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The operating principle of typical MOSFETs AC/DC rectifier is introduced in this paper. In order to maximize the operating range of RFID transponder, low-power design techniques are needed. Therefore, the key design parameters optimization of passive rectifier is discussed. Besides, the design of a low-power rectifier for passive UHF RFID transponder, which is compatible with standard CMOS process and can be applied to the environment in which the distance from interrogator changes greatly, is also presented in this paper. Measurement results showed that if a 510 kilo-ohm resistance is added at the rectifier output and 4 W EIRP interrogator transmit power, the rectifier can output 1.6 V to 2 V DC voltage, the minimum RF input power is about 230 muW corresponding to a reading distance of 3.45 m.

articleTitle: A Non-cooperative Power Control Game Considering Utilization and Fairness in Cognitive Radio Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Power control is one of the key technologies in radio resource management, and efficient power control scheme can decrease the interference to other users and save the power consumption. In cognitive radio network, the interference caused by unlicensed user to licensed user is strictly limited. In order to maximize the network utility, a game theoretic approach is proposed. In this paper, a new power control algorithm with a certain type of price coefficient is proposed based on game theory, and it takes the interference to the licensed users into account. Meanwhile, the algorithm also gives attention to both system capacity and fairness index. We can show the existence and uniqueness of the Nash equilibrium of the proposed algorithm further. In addition, its better performance can be indicated by the numeral results.

articleTitle: Broadband Polarization Diversity Base Station Antenna for 3G Communication System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Antennas with dual linear slant polarization over a wide band are necessary for modern personal communication base-station applications. A plusmn45deg polarization diversity antenna element constructed by novel umbrella-shaped dipoles is presented in this paper. The antenna has a half-power beam width of 63deg plusmn5deg in the horizontal plane by designing a reflector over a bandwidth of 1710 to 2170MHz, which covers not only 3G frequency band(1920-2170MHz) but also DCS band (1710-1880MHz) and PCS band (1850-1990MHz). In addition the worst-case isolation between polarizations is 30dB and the front-to-back ratio is more than 30dB over the above frequency band.

articleTitle: A W-band Low Loss E-plane Type Waveguide Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper present the design for W-band E-plane bandpass waveguide filter based on the equivalent circuit of an inserted strip in the middle of the waveguide broadside. The equivalent network parameters and its transformation are analyzed by the classic filter design theory. Experiment results agree well with the simulation data.

articleTitle: Extraction of Calibration Waveform for Confocal Microwave Imaging for Early Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Microwave imaging is a promising method for the early-stage breast cancer detection based on the large contrast of electric parameters between the tumor and the normal breast tissue. The tumor information can be obtained by comparing the ultra wideband signals propagating in the tumor-contained breast and tumor-free breast which used as the calibration waveform. In this study, a method of extracting calibration waveform during detection is proposed, in which the tumor is arranged randomly located in the breast tissue. The feasibility of this method in the actual detection is explained. The correct tumor information in the reconstructed breast image is achieved by using the extracted calibration waveform.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Selective CQI Feedback Scheme for 3GPP Long-Term Evolution System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In the 3GPP Long term Evolution system, one of the key techniques to meet the performance requirements in the downlink is the frequency selective schedule (FSS), in which resource allocation and modulation and code schemes are changed adaptively according to the downlink channel quality reported by user equipments (IE). Therefore, the channel quality information (CQI) scheme will directly affect the accuracy of the FSS and the system performance. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical selective (HS) CQI feedback scheme where a hierarchical structure is used to divide the whole system band into subbands and only CQI of the subbands with good channel quality is selected to be reported. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can significantly reduce the CQI feedback overhead in the uplink by the cost of little performance degradation in the downlink.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Multifunction Antennas: Next Steps fot the Future
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper reviews the state-of-the-art in reconfigurablc multifunction antenna technology, including antennas with compound reconfigurability and integrated switching mechanisms. System-level demonstrations of some antennas are also highlighted. Possible directions for future research in this area are discussed, with an emphasis on bringing reconfigurable antennas together with other system components to deliver superior system performance.

articleTitle: A Multi-Band Small Antenna Based on Deformed Split Ring Resonators of Left-Handed Meta-Materials
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A multi-band small antenna based on deformed split ring resonators is presented in this paper. The antenna is consisted of a microstrip line and a deformed split square ring which is coplanar with the partly covered ground plane. The antenna has been numerically proved that it possesses three working bands.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Field Uniformity of Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The absorber materials used in anechoic and semi-anechoic chambers and the field uniformity are described in this paper. The field uniformity of anechoic chamber is simulated with software HFSS 10.0, Ansoft. A low frequency model for absorber-arrays is obtained using the method of homogenization. The simulation result testifies the method is feasible.

articleTitle: OFDM Bit and Power Allocation Based on Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: To the problem of bit and power allocation in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a novel framework was proposed which introduced the game theory and a new algorithm was applied. Firstly, the power allocation problem was described as non-cooperative Game process. Secondly, combined with influences of required quality of service (QoS), the frequency efficiency was formulated by a utility function and the cost of resources by a price function. Finally, the objective of power allocation was expressed as maximum net utility for each sub-carrier. Considered the algorithm' s limitations, a second power allocation was assigned, in reaching the optimal performances.

articleTitle: A Novel Waveguide to Microstrip Transition in Millimeter-Wave LTCC Module
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a novel Ka-band rectangular waveguide to microstrip transition in LTCC (low temperature co-fired ceramic) modules is presented. This structure is based on the principle of slot coupling between waveguide and microstrip, and has the metal filled via holes as waveguide walls in LTCC multi-layer substrates. This type of waveguide to microstrip transition eliminates the need for specially shaped LTCC substrate inside the waveguide and is very tolerant to small errors in mechanical misalignment between the LTCC substrate and the rectangular waveguide. This proposed structure is validated by full-wave simulations and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: High-Performance Universal GNSS Antenna Based on SMM Antenna Technology
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A class of high-performance low-cost GNSS antennas that cover all three GNSS services (GPS/GLONASS/Galileo) is presented. The designs are based on the ultra-wideband SMM antenna, which has a phase center inherently more stable with angular and frequency variations than other antenna types. The antenna is low-cost and platform conformable. Size reduction using the slow-wave antenna technology and the magneto-dielectric antenna technology is discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of SAR Jamming Performance
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The basic principles of SAR jamming performance evaluation (JPE) are discussed firstly. A novel evaluation method of SAR jamming performance by combining the subjective evaluation and objective evaluation is proposed. Namely, based on the objective evaluation parameters, a nominal value of SAR jamming performance can be obtained by weighting the objective evaluation parameters, where the weighted factors come from expert's judgments. Detailed derivations are given as well as the simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Tuned S-shaped Resonators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Tunable metamaterials are important for designing of microwave devices. Tuning methods for S- shaped resonators (metamaterial) have been presented in this paper. Simulation results, obtained from FEM based simulator, have been included and are compared with untuned counterpart. Changes in transmission pass bands are observed as a result of tuning.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Broadband Unidirectional CPW-Fed Rectangular Slot Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A broadband unidirectional coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed rectangular slot millimeter wave antenna based on micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) non-silicon micro-fabrication technology is discussed. A wide impedance bandwidth of 75% (Su<-10dB) was obtained. By adding special wave guiding structure and reflecting structure, the antenna achieves unidirectional radiation, and the max gain of the antenna increases from 3. 8 dB to 6. 8 dB. Ansoft HFSS and CST Microwave Studio, two high frequency structure simulation softwares are used to simulate and analyze the antenna performances.

articleTitle: Characteristic and Simulation of the Near Space Communication Channel
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Near space vehicle, the hotspot in the military research currently, has significant strategic value. The paper analyzes the characteristic of the near space communication channel, amends C. Loo' s fading channel model based on Doppler frequency shift, and gives the expressions for the probability density function, the level crossing rate and the average fading duration of the received signal. The expressions for the fading channel of near space communication in light shadowing, heavy shadowing and overall shadowing are respectively calculated numerically by simulation. The paper has great significance on the development and research for near space vehicles.

articleTitle: Efficient Multiuser Water-filling Algorithm under Interference Temperature Constraints in OFDMA-based Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Cognitive radio makes it possible for an unlicensed user to access a spectrum unoccupied by licensed users. Efficient subcarricr and power allocation algorithm in CR networks is a challenging problem, especially for uplink. In this paper, an efficient multiuser water-filling algorithm is proposed under the interference temperature constraints. L'sing this algorithm, subcarriers are allocated to the users with the best channel quality initially and then adjusted to improve the system performance. As is shown in the simulation results, the proposed algorithm has a much lower computational complexity and the performance is close to optimal scheme. Finally, it is proved that there is an upper bound of the throughput loss by using this algorithm.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Parameters Test System Based on A Refined NRW Transmission/Reflection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new refined algorithm is presented based on the traditional NRW transmission/reflection method (T/R method). According to the magnetic property of the material under test, the algorithm can get different solutions, then obtain the complex permittivity and complex permeability of magnetic material simultaneously or the complex permittivity of nonmagnetic material. It solves the half-wavelength divergence problem and the multi-roots problem which exist in the traditional NRW algorithm and overcomes the machining and assembling problem of thin samples which is required in the traditional algorithm. Automatic test software is programmed and the whole test system is established. Tests of air and FIFE are carried out to verify the reliability of this test system and the results are consistent with true values.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution of Polarimetric SAR Images for Ship Detection
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Polarimetric SAR images are used for aerial and space imagery applications, such as target detection, tracking, and resource exploration. However, spatial resolution is limited due to the signal bandwidth and the antenna dimension. Super-resolution reconstruction is the process to reconstruct a high-resolution image from multiple low-resolution images. Polarimetric SAR provides multiple images of the same scene at the different channels (HH, VV, HV and VH). In this paper, the POCS method is applied to extract the information from LR images in different channels to generate the HR image. The multiplicative characteristics of noises in SAR images are utilized to construct the convex sets in POCS method. Ship targets are selected as detection object for super-resolution. Results from simulated and real data have validated the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: An annular-ring slot antenna for circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The design of a novel dual-band annular -ring slot antenna for circular polarization (CP) is presented. The proposed antenna with simple structure is easy to be fabricated and adjusted. Parameters affecting the performance of the antenna are investigated. Details of the simulated results of the CP performance and return loss are presented.

articleTitle: A Novel Adaptive Digital Predistortion for RF Power Amplifier Linearization Based on Simplified Volterra Series
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Adaptive digital predistortion (ADPD) is an effective approach to compensate for nonlinear distortion introduced by RF power amplifiers (PAs). Volterra series is applicable for predistorter design to linearize memory PAs; however, the number of its kernels to be identified increases greatly with its degree and memory length. In this paper, a simplified Volterra series (SVS) predistorter model is proposed. By only preserving partial Volterra kernels in the region near the main diagonal, the structure is simplified and computational complexity is reduced dramatically. Through MATLAB simulations using a Wiener-Hammerstein PA model and a two-carrier WCDMA wideband signal, linearization performances of SVS-based predistorters are demonstrated in terms of suppressing spectral regrowth.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Printed Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact ultra-wide band (UWB) printed antenna is proposed for UWB communication. The simulated return loss is less than -10 dB from 2.45 to 10.3 GHz. The antenna consisted by a square patch and a trident-shaped feeding line. By adding of a bevel on both sides of the feeding line, the bandwidth improved greatly. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits a good cross-polarization by the addition of the bevel. Details of the experimental and simulation results for the proposed planar monopole antenna are presented and analyzed.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Demodulation Method for QAM Signals
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents a novel method for demodulating the QAM signals basing on adaptive filtering. The commonly used least mean square (LMS) error adaptive filtering algorithm is employed for studying the demodulating procedure and the performance of the novel adaptive QAM demodulation. The novel adaptive QAM demodulation does not need the adaptive filter completing convergence. Therefore, the sampling rate and processing speed are decelerated. The performance of the method in theory is compared with computer simulating results. It shows that the error rates in simulation agree well with that in theory. Also, it is indicated that the demodulation method has many advantages over conventional ones, such as the powerful anti-noise ability, the small transfer delay, and the convenient implementation with DSP technology.

articleTitle: Using Neural Network Classifier of Packet Loss Causes to Improve TCP Congestion Control over Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A backpropagation neural network cIassifier is used for distinguishing network congestion and link error over ad hoc networks. TCP considers a 11 packet losses as network congestion, and reacts to such congestion by reducing its data rate. In ad hoc networks, there are many packet losses are due to Iink errors, but not due to network congestion; and then TCP often reduces its data rate mistakenly, cannot keep a reasonable data rate. Then we introduce an improvement TCP with a packet loss classifier, TCP-BP algorithm. The result of our simulation shows that the TCP-BP algorithm is superior to Vegas and TCP Westwood algorithm in TCP throughput.

articleTitle: EMC Design for HEV Drive System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Recently, hybrid electric vehicle entered a high-speed developing period. EMC design of HEV electrical system become more important than any other time. In this paper, the authors shows a image of internal electromagnetic environment of HEV electrical system. They give the methods to minimize the electromagnetic interference, analysis and design the driving system with detailed practical technique.

articleTitle: A Method to Improve the Performance of the Stacked Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The configuration of the truncated-corners square patch antenna with a single feed is simple and easy to fabricate. Therefore, it has been applied broadly in GPS antennas. However, this kind of configuration has narrow axial ratio bandwidth, poor performance of circular polarization (CP) operation for low-elevation angles. This paper describes the method to improve the quality of the circular polarized axial ratio of the stacked antenna. Details of the proposed antenna design are described, and experimental results for the CP performance are presented.

articleTitle: ESPRIT algorithm for joint delay and 2-dimensional DOA estimation of multipath parameters
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for the simultaneous estimation of the 2D arrival angles and the path delays of emitted user signals. By using the ESPRIT algorithm, we firstly formulate the problem with 3 matrix pencil pairs, where the eigenvalues of the matrix pencils contain the unknown parameters. Then a pairing free algorithm is developed to solve the matrix pencil based 3D estimation problem. The new algorithm results in automatical pairing of the parameters in different pencil and thus avoids a separate pairing operation.

articleTitle: Improvements of Robustness of Genetic Algorithm for Near Field - Far Field Radiation Conversion
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The robustness of genetic algorithm in finding equivalent ideal electric and magnetic dipoles for near field-far field radiation conversion is improved. The process of selection, crossover and mutation is investigated in detail for solving the sticking problem, and the performance of genetic algorithm is evaluated.

articleTitle: Compact Reconfigurable Microstrip Antenna For Multi-band Wireless Appications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna with very wide operational bandwidth is presented. The proposed design consists of a rectangular patch loaded with varactor diodes at the radiating edges and meandered with slits at the non-radiating edges. With capacitance of the varactor diodes being varied, the operational frequency of the antenna is tunable in the range of 1.79-2.71 GHz that covers DCS/PCS/UMTS/ISM wireless communication bands. Simulation results show that good performance can be achieved.

articleTitle: 2-D Frequency Spectrum Features and Error Analysis for Interferometric Passive Microwave Imager
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces the basic concepts of interferometric passive microwave imager (aperture synthesis interferometric radiometers), and presents several features of 2D frequency spectrum. On basis of those features, the directions and positions of baselines with errors can be identified approximately. And the effects caused by several systematic errors (antenna position error, baseline absence, amplitude error and phase error in channels, and antenna pattern error) on the reconstructed images, are analyzed particularly. The analyses in the paper can provide the evidences to identify the error types and sources in interferometric passive microwave imager, and can supply important references to design enhancement algorithms.

Author Keywords: Interferometric Passive Microwave Imager(Aperture Synthesis Interferometric Radiometers)
amplitude error and phase error in channel

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Improving Bandwidth of a Printed CPW-fed FIFA
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel printed planar invert-F antenna (PIFA) is developed. By introducing a parasitical radiation element, this novel antenna achieves a wider impedance bandwidth than that of a traditional PIFA. The printed antenna is fed by a simple coplanar waveguide (CPW) structure that can provide consistent characteristic impedance over a very wide bandwidth. A prototype of the proposed antenna has been constructed and tested. Details of the simulation and experimental results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: An Effective Fast Matching Oriented Slot Antenna Designing Method with RFID Tag Chip
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: One of the important factors that determine the performance of RFID (radio frequency identification) system is whether the design of the RFID tag antenna is able to achieve an effective matching between the antenna and its chip. The paper studies how the changes of antenna's geometry parameters affect both real and imaginary part of impedance of slot antenna by using the MOM (Method of Moment) and then presents an effective method, which achieves quick and effective matching through changing the geometry parameters of the bent slot antenna. The paper further validates its method by designing a slot antenna for a set of chips at 915 MHz frequency band through simulation. The test results show that the matching between slot antenna and tag chip has high matching speed, high efficiency and excellent directivity. And the test also proves 'hat the antenna satisfies the RFID application requirements. All these results further validate the reliability of the presented matching method.

articleTitle: Improved Particle Swarm to Nonlinear Blind Source Separation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper propose the nonlinear blind source separation algorithm using improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) combined with natural gradient algorithm. The model of nonlinear blind source separation (NBSS) is built which the nonlinear transfer function is simulate by the P-th order polynomial function. At the same time, Based on the character of particle swarm optimization (PSO), "migrating operator" and local area deep-searching is introduce into PSO. Then, the parameters of the P-th order polynomial function is estimated by PSO. Experimental results indicate that tire established algorithm of PSO can quickly and effectively get optimal resolution to the nonlinear blind source separation.

articleTitle: A Novel RX-TX Front-Ends for Passive RFID Reader with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In passive radio frequency identification (RFID) system, the isolation between transmitter and receiver has been a critical problem because the TX and RX are simultaneous. A directional coupler has been used to isolate RX from TX, whereas some latent disadvantage of insertion loss of receiver signal and poor isolation have already emerged from conventional microstrip directional coupler because of low coupling and unequal phase velocity between even and odd mode. In this paper, a new RX-TX Front-Ends based on a 3dB branch-line coupler is proposed to reduce the insertion loss of the received signal and improve the isolation by Reflected Power Canceller (RPC) between TX and RX. The results of the proposed method show that the insertion loss of received signal is about 3dB and the transmit/receive isolation is more than 46dB in the UHF RFID frequency band.

articleTitle: Microstrip Wide Band-pass Filter Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW)
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel microstrip wide band-pass filter using the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technique (K. Wu et al., 2003) is described in this paper. The SIW is one of alternatives for packaging the microwave components on the same substrate. The filter exhibits 52.7% bandwidth (6.67 GHz-11.45 GHz in the center frequency 9.06 GHz) for -10.2 dB return loss and 2.3 dB insertion loss in the pass-band. The proposed filter has a compact size and it is suitable for designing microwave and millimeter-wave circuits.

articleTitle: Compact Printed Monopole Antenna with Super-wideband
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact semi-elliptical patch antenna fed by a tapered coplanar waveguide (CPW) is presented. The simulated and experimental results demonstrate that the antenna possesses the desirable super-wideband (SWB) characteristics, achieving a ratio bandwidth of 19.7:1 for VSWRles2, and exhibits a nearly omni-directional radiation pattern, while its area is only about 0.15 lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> times 0.2 1 lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, where lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> is the wavelength of the lowest operating frequency.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Extraction of Micro-Doppler Signal
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The micro-Doppler effect may be generated by additional frequency modulations on the returned radar signal if the target contains rotating structures. The body image will be contaminated duo to the existence of the micro-Doppler. In the paper, a simple method based on integral of dwell-time is introduced, which can be utilized to separate the signal of the rotating parts from that of the target body successfully. It makes the ISAR image clearer and also provides some information of the rotating parts, such as the radii and the rotation frequencies. Computer simulations are given to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Energy-saving Strategies of Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSN), which consist of randomly deployed tiny sensors, data processing unit, and communicating components, have a wide range of applications, such as industry, agriculture, business, military, and health. Because power supply might be impossible, it is the key problem to find an efficient energy strategy for prolonging network's lifetime. This article made a detailed introduction for energy management of WSN, analyzing energy strategies used for WSN.

articleTitle: Recent Development of Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Filters
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper aims to reports the recent progress in developing UWB filters. Several advanced UWB filter structures are demonstrated with electromagnetic (EM) simulated and experimental results.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Resource Allocation Scheme Based on Soft Frequency Reuse for OFDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we present a dynamic resource allocation algorithm, termed Dynamic Major group Allocation (DMA), based on Soft Frequency Reuse (SFR) which is an efficient method to mitigate inter-cell interference (ICI) in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA) systems. DMA defines the method that Radio Network Controller (RNC) orthogonally assigns resource to Cell Edge Users (CEU) in neighboring cells (or sectors) firstly, and then each cell allocal.es its residual resource to Cell Center Users (CCU) according to PF scheduling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DMA algorithm carries superior throughput performance of CEU over the traditional two-level resource allocation scheme (TLA) which simply combines SFR with PF.

articleTitle: Performance and analysis of CML Logic gates and latches
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A feedback MOS current mode logic (MCML) is proposed for the high-speed operation of CMOS transistors. This logic is more tolerant to the threshold voltage fluctuation than the conventional MCML and is suitable for gigahertz operation of deep-submicron CMOS transistors. In this work, MOS current mode logic (MCML) is analyzed for application to low power, mixed signal environments. A small MCML cell library is developed and optimized for several different performance requirements. The cells are then applied to the generation of logic gates and latch structures and compared with equivalent CMOS circuits. Experimental results show a higher performance for the new latch architectures compared to the conventional CML latch circuit at ultrahigh- frequencies. It is also shown, both through the experiments and by using efficient analytical models, why CML buffers are better than CMOS inverters in high-speed low-voltage applications.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Microstrip-Fed Bow-Tie Antenna for GSM/CDMA and 3G/WLAN
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A dual-band microstrip-fed bow-tie antenna printed on dielectric substrate of epsiv<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> =2. 2 is designed to operate at the GSM/CDMA bands from 800MHz to 960MHz and the 3G/WLAN bands from 1.7GHz to 2. 5GHz. This novel antenna exhibits good performances as desired in mobile telecommunication applications. The designed bow-tie antenna was fabricated and measured, showing a good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Propagation Path Loss Characterization for An 870 MHz Cellular CDMA System in Taipei City
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents the significant measurement results on wave propagation characteristics at an 870 MHz (CDMA2000 band) cellular system in Taipei city, dense urban environments. Furthermore, observed field strength values are converted into path loss and are compared with different path loss prediction methods Hata and COST 231 Walfisch-Ikegami. It's apparent the measured propagation path loss in Taipei city is higher at 0~5dB (dependent on distances) than the two models. Our study also indicates that expression used in Lee model in some previous papers needs to be corrected.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Classification of Polarimetric SAR Images by Gamma-Correction of Features using Self Organizing Map
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Unsupervised classification algorithms have tendency to form more clusters in the upper range of tin- features used for classification. In case of polarimetric SAR.. this means that, different areas having low polarimetric response will be merged into a single cluster and an area with large polarimetric response will be segmented into many clusters. This, for example, occurs in the areas like water, grass, roads and ot her flat surfaces which, owing to t heir low polarimetric response, are often assigned to the same cluster. Urban areas and other man-made objects, on the other hand, generally have large polarimetric response, and have tendency to form more clusters than required. To avoid this, we scale the features by applying gamma-correct ion or a power law transformation to nonlinearly reduce the dynamic range of features. A gamma-corrected feature has a more evenly distributed histogram as compared to the untransformed feature. In the transformed feature space thus obtained, the areas with low polarimetric response are mapped to a larger range of the total range as compared to the input feature space. This transformation of the feature space may provide a chance to the clustering algorithm to separate the low polarimetric response areas from each other. A neural network based on self organizing map (SOM) is used to classify I lie polarimetric SAR image into different clusters. A variety of features have been utilized to form the feature vectors. Elements of the polarimetric coherency matrix, derived features like Freeman decompositions. Alpha, Entropy. Anisotropy, and Eigen values of the coherency matrix may be used. The results show the comparison of the images classified by using both transformed and untransformed features.

articleTitle: Test on Lightning Characteristics of Electronic Equipment's Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, lightning characteristics of electronic equipment power supply are studied. Firstly impulse generator is developed. Then lightning characteristics tests for different power supply, such as switch model power supply, are done. Test results show: different power supply has different lightning impulse characteristics.Usually two different models are used for lightning performance evaluation: common and different model. Both impulse current and impulse voltage withstand capability in common model are stronger than those in different model. Flashover often occurs in the AC-DC conversion part inside of the switch power supply when there is lightning stroke. The manufacturing technology of the power supply has definite effect on withstand capability. The switch model power supply has some weak parts when there is lightning stroke, such as transformers in the AC-DC conversion part, the resistor and capacitor of the bridge rectifier. Switch model power supply have stronger lightning withstand capability than common small power supply we chose as equipment under test. It is necessary to measure lightning withstand capability when designing lightning protection system for power supply in low voltage electronic equipments. The data presented in this paper could provide reference for real situation.

articleTitle: Cross-layer Design for Adaptive Modulation and Coding with Hybrid ARQ
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An important aspect of wireless networks is the dynamic behavior, cross-layer design is the central technique to cope with and utilize this behavior. In this paper, we present the cross-layer design for adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) with HARQ. For each of two widely used HARQ techniques-chase combining and incremental redundancy, the close-form functions of average retransmission time, average delay and average throughput are derived for a specific modulation and coding scheme (MCS). Based on the derived functions, a novel MCS selection method is proposed. Meanwhile, we give the analysis of how many retransmission is needed.

articleTitle: Research on Subarray Partitioning of Planar Phased Array with Adaptive Digital Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An approach of subarray partitioning for planar phase array radars with ADBF is presented. The architecture of subarray is optimized using genetic algorithm. With the optimized structure of the array, the sidelobe level of adaptive pattern has been well improved; meanwhile, the jammer was suppressed obviously in the direction of the jammer arrival for ADBF at the subarray level. That was demonstrated on 30x32 elements planar array.

articleTitle: Multiuser Scheduling Analysis of MIMO STBC with Imperfect Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) system has captured considerably attention recently. In this paper, we present the analysis of multiuser scheduling in MIMO space-time block coding (STBC) system with imperfect channel estimation. Three commonly used multiuser scheduling methods - max throughput, round robin (RR) and proportional fair (PF) - are implemented to the MIMO STBC system and their performances are analyzed with imperfect channel estimation. Numerical and simulation results are provided to show multiuser diversity and the impact of imperfect channel estimation on the multiuser scheduling performance in MIMO STBC systems. The simulation results show that more multiuser diversity gain is obtained as the increase of user number and the channel estimation errors has a great impact on the performance of max throughput and PF methods.

Index Terms: Increase In The Number Of Users

articleTitle: A Widely-Linear LMS Algorithm for Adaptive Beamformer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel adaptive Array structure using widely-linear weight is proposed in this paper. MMSE law is used to evaluate the performance of the adaptive array. According to the widely-linear structure, the widely-linear LMS algorithm (WL-LMS) is used here, which uses widely-linear model of the received signal rather than linear model estimating the desired signal. This structure provides a unified framework for beamforming in circular and non-circular sources, and can get much less MMSE between the beamforming output and the desired signal. This algorithm has been tested for beamforming using BPSK and narrow-band FM signal.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of the Eighth Sub-Harmonic Mixers at W-band
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, design of an eighth sub-harmonic (SH) mixer at W-band using microstrip transmission lines is introduced. According to concretely analyzing, another improved eighth SH mixer is designed. The measurement results show that its best conversion loss is about 10 dB less than the first one. In addition, the bandwidth of RF frequency is 10 GHz (90-100 GHz). In addition; the structure of the improved one is simpler than the original one.

articleTitle: Double Ridged Waveguide Low Pass Filters for Satellite application
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Waveguide low pass filters (LPFs) are used widely in satellite payload for its stop-band performance. Design procedure for double ridged waveguide LPF with wider stop-band is presented in this paper, the rectangular and ridged waveguide discontinuity junctions are simulated by modal S- matrix method, and such waveguide junctions and waveguide sections are cascaded to obtain the whole S-parameters of LPF. Final, the structure parameters of LPF are achieved through optimization. As an example, a Ku-band double ridged waveguide LPF is realized, and the measured response agree well with the predicted values.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-cost Active RFID Platform
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Active RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) systems have attracted considerable attention in recent years because it long operating range. In this study, we propose a new design and implementation of an active RFID platform which operates at 2.45 GHz Industrial Scientific Medical (ISM) band. The hardware design of the tag and interrogator is introduced in detail. Moreover, communication protocol of energy saving mechanism and anti-collision is presented. Performance evaluation shows a long lifetime of the battery and a good identification performance of the presented platform. All used components in this platform are commercial-off-the-shelf components, which makes the platform cheap and be flexible for many kinds of applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupled or Single Nonuniform Transmission Lines Using the Equivalent Sources Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A method is proposed for analysis of arbitrarily loaded lossy and dispersive single or coupled nonuniform transmission lines (NTLs). In this method, the equations of coupled NTLs are converted to the equations of coupled uniform transmission lines, which have been excited by distributed equivalent sources. The modal decomposition approach is used to decouple the sets of differential equations. Then, the voltage and current distributions are obtained using an iterative approach. The validity of the method is verified using an example.

articleTitle: Wideband Channel Measurements and Characterization of the Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper studied the small-scale multipath propagation characteristics of the wireless channel at 3.5GHz, in a typical outdoor urban environment. A channel measurement platform was developed for the measurement. Both the fixed and mobile scenarios were measured; the power delay profile, the tapped delay line model, the multipath distribution, the mean excess delay and the Ricean K-factor were presented in the paper. The results verify that it is a rich scattered environment fit for multiple antenna wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Ka Band Transceiver Using LTCC Technology
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A Ka band transceiver based on low temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC) technology is presented in this paper. All the passive elements as well as naked millimeter-wave MMICs of the module are integrated in standard multi-layer LTCC, and encapsulated in metallic package with the size of 30 mm X 30 mm X 4. 5 mm. The measured results demonstrate the feasibility of developing highly miniaturized and hermetical package transceivers at Ka band.

articleTitle: The Design of 3.6GHz 4.2GHz Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A two-stage broadband low noise amplifier (LNA) was designed. The LNa was implemented on a Teflon substrate using GaAs FET ATF-10136 and PHEMT ATF-34143 with micro-strip circuit technology. This LNA resulted in a noise figure of 1.1dB, and 21 dB gain over 3.6 to 4.2 GHz range. The input and output VSWR are all less than 2.8. The computer simulated results were coincident with that of the test.

articleTitle: Subthreshold Characteristic of Double-gate Accumulation-mode SOI PMOSFET
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, an analytical model of subthreshold swing for the double-gate accumulation-mode P-channel SOI MOSFET is described. The model is based on Possion's equation and depletion approximation, and the relation of the subthreshold swing with both the gate oxide capacitance and the interface trap density is obtained. The model is verified by experiment and by numerical simulation. Also an approach to extracting the interface trap density with subthreshold swing is proposed.

articleTitle: A New 2-D DOA Estimation Algorithm for Noncircular Signals
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel 2D direction finding algorithm for noncircular signals using two parallel linear arrays called extended rank reduction (ERARE) algorithm is presented in this paper. The proposed method needs only 1D search for joint azimuth and elevation estimation. The 2D angles estimated by ERARE are paired automatically. The estimation precision of 2D angles by ERARE algorithm is better than the DOA matrix (DOAM) algorithm which is also a 2D direction finding algorithm with dual parallel subarrays.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Probe-fed Cylindrically Conformal Microstrip Patch Antenna using the Conformal FDTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The conformal FDTD algorithm is employed to analyze the characteristics of a probe-fed cylindrically conformal microstrip patch antenna. A hybrid technique in Cartesian coordinate system combining the non-uniform meshing and matrix-pencil approach is used to obtain the input impedance and the radiation pattern of the above-mentioned antenna. The numerical results show that the conformal algorithm is efficient and accurate enough, besides its better adaptability in dealing with arbitrary antenna structures and shapes.

articleTitle: The Analysis And Simulation Research of Distance Resolution and Ambiguity Property of LFM Signal
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The linear frequency modulation signal with bigger time-bandwidth product which is widely used in the pulse compression system radar. This paper is according to characteristic of the linear frequency modulation signal, and use the ambiguity function theory to analyse the characteristic. Gave out the course and result of the linear frequency modulation signal through matched filter. Hamming weighting the matched filter output response and simulation the output signal through weighting, and analyses the influence of window function to the matched filter output response and the distance resolution .

articleTitle: A Simple Design Method for Nonuniform Cosine Modulated Filter Banks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Traditional designs for nonuniform filter banks usually involve complicated nonlinear optimization with a large number of parameters. A simple design approach that involves the optimization of only single parameter is presented for the design of nonuniform cosine modulated filter bank, which is derived by combination of filters in uniform cosine modulated filter banks. The prototype filter is formulated as an interpolated FIR filter and is indirectly designed by varying the passband edge of a low-order model filter. A design example is presented to show that very good design can be obtained in spite of the limit of the formulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Mobility Management Scheme for Convergence of Heterogeneous Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: With fast development of wireless technologies, we are getting more and more focused on the issue how to provide ubiquitous services over various current wireless networks, namely convergence of heterogeneous networks. In the environment of heterogeneous wireless networks, it is indispensable to support seamless mobility between these wireless networks, for the purpose of perfect services provision. Traditional mobility management has already become incapable to support mobility in heterogeneous wireless networks. Considering from application layer, network layer and wireless access layer comprehensively, this paper presents a novel mobility management scheme based on cross-layer theory. And then this scheme is detailed with the example of interworking among WLAN, GSM/GPRS and UMTS.

articleTitle: Zero-Watermark Scheme Based on Audio's Statistical Character
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: a new zero-watermark algorithm based on audio's statistical character is presented. By using the audio's statistical character, this paper consults the mean of the approximation coefficients of a one-dimensional signal and constructs the watermark sequence within the zero-watermark scheme. By this way, it is efficient to resolve the required trade-off between the robustness to certain watermark attacks and the imperceptual quality. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed watermarking algorithm is greatly imperceptible and robust against general malicious attacks.

articleTitle: A compact bandpass filter with two finite transmission zeros using LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact quasi-lumped parameter bandpass filter structure using low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology is proposed. Filters with this structure can have small size and realize transmission zeros in the stop band. A bandpass filter with center frequency at 1.2 GHz is designed in this paper . The simulation response exhibits an insertion loss of 0. 46 dB, a return loss of 17 dB, and a relative band width of 8% . Two transmission zeros are realized at 0.61 GHz and 2.11 GHz, with suppression larger than 43 dB.

articleTitle: Image Coding Algorithm Based on All Phase Walsh Biorthogonal Transform
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes new concepts of the all phase Walsh biorthogonal transform (APWBT) and the dual biorthogonal basis vectors based on the Walsh-Hadamard transform. The matrices of APWBT are deduced. They can be used in image compression instead of the discrete cosine transform (DCT). Compared with DCT in JPEG image compression algorithm, the PSNRs of the reconstructed images using the transform are the same as DCT's at the same bit rates, but the advantage is that the quantization is very simple. The transform coefficients can be quantized uniformly. Therefore the computational complexity is reduced and it is much easier to realize with the hardware.

articleTitle: Interference Analysis and Co-existence Studies of 3GPP LTE Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) technology is applied into the 3GPP Long Terra Evolution (LTE) systems. Based on the characteristics of frequency assignment and transmission scheme, the interference and compatibility related to co-existence of LTE is highlighted in this paper. The radio frequency (RF) system scenarios and the LTE-specific co-existence studies methodology are presented. The performance degradation due to the co-existence is quantified by comparing with single system scenarios and optimal co-existence compromise has also been derived in this paper.

articleTitle: The Research of Phase Center of Log-periodic dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper researches a method about obtaining phase center of the log-periodic dipole antenna, and verifies the result mainly through commercial electromagnetic simulation software and the analysis of variance. In the process of verification, variance is used to find the correctness of the phase center by computing to obtain a small fluctuation. Thus compare the result through directly simulating and the results of the analysis method to achieve the purpose of validation. At the same time, the mathematical model of the analysis of variance is established. All relevant factors affecting the result of the trial by analyzing data will gain. With the series of computing, verifying and analyzing, the phase center of log-periodic dipole antenna is accurately and effectively found in order to guide the practice.

articleTitle: A New Method for m-sequence and Gold-sequence Generator Polynomial Estimation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A finite field discrete Fourier transform is used for studying the properties of linear feedback shift register (LFSR) sequence with period (q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-1)/n, and the elation of sequence' s linear complexity and the nonzero-points in frequency-domain is given in this paper. Then a new algorithm is introduced to estimate the generator polynomial and initial state of m-sequence and gold-sequence. Based on the principle of FFT, a fast algorithm is also explored.

articleTitle: Design of Broad-Band Circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized microstrip antenna array is presented in this paper. This array has 8X8 elements and a parallel feed networks. The whole size of this X band array is 190mm X 190mm X 0.787mm. The measurement of the bandwidth of this array is 7.32% (VSWR<2), the gain is about 24dB and the axial ratio is less than 3dB in the operating band. This single layer microstrip antenna array is promising in application because of its compact size and excellent characteristics.

articleTitle: The Detection and Tracking of Weak Frequency Line Based on Double-detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper aims to deal with the problem of automatic detection of narrow-band signals which is encountered in a passive sonar system. The double-detection algorithm at low signal-to-noise ratio is put forward on a basis of double-thresholds detection, and realizes the intelligence methods of frequency line detection and tracking. It makes frequency line detection and tracking more intelligent. The results of experimental data processing reveal that this method can increase the possibility of weak frequency line detection and tracking, and decrease the false alarm rate.

articleTitle: Visualization of High Dynamic Range Image with Retinex Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Nowadays, high dynamic range (HDR) radiance maps are becoming increasingly common and important in computer graphics. Meanwhile, HDR images of real scenes are very easy to construct. But the limitations of display devices are more and more exposed. This paper addresses the problem of high dynamic range scenes visualization and proposes the Retinex algorithm to enhance the rendering of high dynamic range images. The image is repeatedly processed with a ratio-product-reset-average operation. Applications of the algorithm to various high dynamic range color images yield promising results compared to the logarithmic transformation rendering algorithm. Moreover, variance and average gradient are proposed to evaluate the performance of this algorithm.

articleTitle: A New UWB Skeletal Antenna for EMC Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a new UWB antenna structure is introduced for EMC applications. This antenna is the skeletal form of the teardrop antenna. As the frequency decreases, the usual teardrop antenna is not applicable since the weight of such antenna as well as its ground dimension considerably increases and such antenna has not a good resistance against the wind. The performance of the proposed antenna is compared with another member of wire UWB antennas' family which is called wire biconical antenna. The results show that the proposed antenna, in comparison to the wire biconical one, has considerably better VSWR especially in the lower band of operation.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Patterns on Narrowband MIMO Capacity
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a model for MIMO capacity calculation with array element radiation patterns is proposed. The proposed model considers effect of radiation pattern, channel impulse responses and elements correlation separately. The effects of both directional and omni-directional antennas to the MIMO capacity are investigated. For the directional antenna case, horizontal polarized Dipole and Yagi-uda antennas are employed in the array. The omni-directional antennas case is considered to be an ideal MIMO capacity. We have shown that directional antennas reduce the narrowband MIMO capacity when the angle of arrival (AOA) is uniformly distributed. When the directional antennas with proper alignment to the mean AOA are used in a scenario where the AOA is Laplacian distribution, the capacity is increased. However, if the antenna alignment is off from the mean AOA, then the capacity is decreased.

articleTitle: Study on V-Shaped Dipole Antenna Array for Pulse Radiation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Time-domain electric field integral equation method is used to obtain the transient current distribution and the far field of V-shaped dipole antenna array in this paper. The time-domain characteristics and the beam steering capability of V-shaped dipole antenna array are studied under new definitions based on energy for time-domain radiation. The beam can be steered into a given direction by properly controlling the time delay of the driving pulses fed to each element.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis and optimization for high-speed circuit systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes a new technique by which circuit matrix equations of high-speed circuits can be formulated directly and we need not consider the matrix forms of distributed parameters. Then sensitivity analysis and optimization of high-speed circuits are derived from the technique. The proposed sensitivity analysis method can be applied with respect to both electrical and physical parameters of multiconductor transmission lines and it is of high efficiency. Minimax technique is applied to the optimization and the effect is obvious, but trying several different initial values is needed. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of these methods and illustrate their application to the sensitivity analysis and optimization of high-speed circuits.

articleTitle: Study of Radar Target Identification Based on Cepstrum and Complex Cepstrum
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A cepstrum analysis based method for radar target identification is proposed firstly. The traditional one nearest-neighbor classifier is used as a classitier. The computer simulation shows that the correct identification rate based on complex cepstrum and cepstrum feature is batter than that based on spectrum.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Power Divider Using Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Left-handed transmission lines (LHTLs) are used in this letter to design a novel Wilkinson power divider. In our design, the lumped L-C LHTLs (-λ/4) is instead of the right-handed transmission lines which is used as branch arms of the conventional Wilkinson power divider. The simulated results show that the novel power divider has a wide bandwidth of return loss and isolation, and its size is 50% smaller than conventional Wilkinson power dividers. The novel Wilkinson power divider has many advantages over conventional power divider in e.g. the size, weight, simplicity, low insertion loss, bandwidth of isolation, and cost.

articleTitle: On Scheduling and Resource Allocation in Multicarrier TD-HSDPA
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we proposed three scheduling and resource allocation schemes for multicarrier TD-SCDMA HSDPA (Multicarrier TD-HSDPA) system. The scheduling algorithms in these schemes are based on proportional fairness (PF) algorithm, which have been modified for systems with multiple carriers to maximize the frequency selective gain in Multicarrier TD-HSDPA system. We modeled Multicarrier TD-HSDPA system in a dynamic system-level simulator, and from the simulation result we can see how the proposed scheduling and resource allocation schemes dig out the potential gain of multiuser diversity in Multicarrier TD-HSDPA to achieve higher spectral efficiency.

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: Measurement of Isolation between Antennas Mounted on Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: To resolve the problem of measurement criterion of isolation between antennas for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design and acceptance test on electronic warfare (EW) special aircraft, two kinds of measurement methods and correlative data processing method, frequency range selection, open area test technologies, errors analysis, etc. are investigated based on factors of energy transmission are analyzed. The application in research and development of models approved that these methods make the measurement process of isolation between antennas normative on EW special aircraft. It is of value to engineering application.

articleTitle: Consideration on accuracy and efficiency of two-scale polarimetric emissivity model used for oceanic passive microwave remote sensing
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Oceanic emission and scattering model is critical in remote sensing wind vector using passive polarimetric microwave radiometer. The brightness temperature emitted from the ocean is mainly determined by the surface roughness, the sea surface temperature, and the dielectric constant of the seawater. The emissivity of rough surface can be calculated by two-sacle model. In this paper, we first dedicate to discuss the effects of some parameters on model calculations, and then we discuss a method to improve the accuracy and efficiency in emissivity simulation, revise Johnson[2006]' s newly published model using our method. The results by compared it with experiments models prove that the revised model is not only accurate enough, but also lower computationally time.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Folded Printed Inverted-F Antenna for Bluetooth Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel microstrip-fed folded planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is proposed in this letter. It is implemented by printing radiating conductors on an FR4 phone main board. A prototype with a small area of 16×4.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has been constructed and analyzed. It is found that the 10-dB impedance bandwidth is approximately 5% centered at 2.45GHz, with reasonable agreement between simulation and measurement. The proposed antenna is extraordinarily suitable for Bluetooth application (2.400-2.484 GHz).

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Loaded Open Sleeve Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A study of Miniaturized Loaded Open Sleeve Antenna is made. In this paper, a top load is applied to lower the height of the antenna; and the open sleeve configuration is applied to miniaturize the area of the ground plane; then load technologies arc applied to broaden the bandwidth of the antenna. Finally, a broadband monopole antenna, with VSWR<3. 0 in 0.4f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>~1.6 f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, is designed, and the results of test fit those of simulation well.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Microstrip Passive Circuits by Field-Based Equivalent Circuit Model with Aggressive Space Mapping
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The field-based equivalent circuit model is applied to the design and optimization of microstrip passive circuits with aggressive space mapping (ASM) technique. The field-based equivalent circuit model is taken as coarse model, while the commercial software IE3D is used as the fine model. Three practical passive components, i.e., two low-pass filters and a power divider, are designed by the field-based equivalent circuit model with ASM. Good convergence performance is achieved for the designs of all examples.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation for MC-CDMA System with Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm is proposed for uplink MC-CDMA system with antenna array. By utilizing the orthogonality of spreading codes and frequency diversity of MC-CDMA the users' signals are separated and enhanced, and the multiple access interference (MAI) is suppressed.
