articleTitle: Antenna Technology for Meteor Scatter Communication
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper analyzes the antenna technology for Meteor Scatter communication, and the characteristics of several antenna patterns are analyzed. Anew system which is useable at both short and long ranges meteor scatter communication is presented, and corresponding antenna patterns are studied.

articleTitle: Gateway Assisted Hybrid Geographic Forwarding for Heterogeneous Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: As more and more innovative applications of wireless sensor networks emerge, the need for deploying heterogeneous sensors for fine-grain monitoring of physical environments subjected to critical conditions rise rapidly. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid forwarding technique based on geographical location with the assistance of gateway node to satisfy performance needs of such applications. The simulation results show that our proposed protocol can achieve better performance both in terms of message latency and energy consumption by appropriately utilizing long-haul asymmetric transmission.

articleTitle: Connector Optimization in Virtual Backbone Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Connected dominating set (CDS) has been proposed as virtual backbone or spine of wireless ad hoc networks. In this paper, we propose a new algorithm optimizing connector number in CDS. Our algorithm tightens upper bound of connector/dominator to 3:1, compared with original algorithm. Even though the new algorithm needs some extra information, its time and message complexity does not increase. In addition, the new algorithm still keeps important properties in [5] but with less interference when applied to multi-radio scenario.

articleTitle: On the Pilot-Symbol Aided Channel Estimation Analysis of Cyclic Delay Diversity for OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Cyclic delay diversity (CDD) is a suggested spatial diversity transmission scheme applied in OFDM system to mitigate intersymbol interference while optimizing channel bandwidth. The increased diversity in the frequency domain caused by the cyclic delays renders channel estimation difficult. In this paper we investigate the effect of pilot-symbol aided channel estimation of CDD-OFDM systems, considering two approaches: first the zero pilot pattern which uses all available pilot simultaneously; second the non-zero pattern where pilots are allocated for each transmit antenna exclusively. The wiener filter is derived for the two approaches. Performance is presented in terms of the bit error rate (BER) and mean square estimation (MSE) obtained from computer simulation.

articleTitle: Realization of the Algorithms of a Multi-static TWSR
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The normal through-the-wall surveillance radar (TWSR) usually has one transmitting antenna (TA and one receiving antenna (RA), which is called monostatic TWSR. In this paper, a multi-static TWSR with one RA and many TAs is presented and this kind of TWSR works more efficiently than the normal one. FDTD method is used to numerically simulate the TWSR system and relative experiments have done. Besides, imaging process is carried out successfully on data of numerical simulation and imitating experiments of the multi-static TWSR by way of diffraction summation algorithm and frequency-wave number (f-k) algorithm.

articleTitle: A Fast and Accurate Frequency Acquisition Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: To aim at short-time pilot pulse carrier- frequency synchronization, a ,fast and accurate acquisition method is proposed. The method employs phase deduction frequency estimator (PDFE) and digital down conversion loop to perform initial and accurate frequency acquisition. The PDFE estimation accuracy exceeds Prony' s method. Its estimation error normalized variance approaches the Cramer-Rao bound of real sinusoid signal at high signal-to-noise ratio. A Simulink simulation model of accurate frequency acquisition loop was established to verify the acquisition accuracy. An example is given, the maximum acquisition error is not more than 2.2 Hz at input SNR above 13 dB.

articleTitle: A New ICCG Method of Large-Scale Sparse Linear Equation Group
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Coefficient matrix of linear equations from finite element method (FEM) is sparse and symmetrical. For the sake of CPU operational time saving to accesses data in matrix decomposition and reducing storing requirement to computer, we introduce fully sparse strategy that stores only nonzero elements of symmetrical part by chain pattern management. Based on the incomplete Cholesky decomposition with thresholds, a new ICCG method is obtained by modifying diagonal elements. The new method can ensure that solution is exact and high-performance. Numerical examples show that the combination of ICCG method and fully sparse storage structure can greatly improve the algorithmic efficiency for FEM solution of large scaled sparse linear equation group.

articleTitle: Estimating Radiated Emission via Conducted Analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the method of estimating radiated emission via calculating the cable' s radiation was discussed. A simple current model was established and the field generated by the current was computed theoretically. A measurement was put forward then in order to check the analysis. The difference between the results gained by computation and measurement respectively was analyzed and the feasibility of this method was discussed.

articleTitle: Partial Soft Layered Group Space-Time MUD in MIMO CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a novel layered group space- time multiuser detection (MUD) with the assistance of partial soft information (PSI) for the uplink of multiple- input multiple output (MIMO) code division multiple access (CDMA) systems. The proposed MUD first employs a simple channel-strength criterion to order the groups. Thereafter, it conducts a block layer cancellation scheme to remove the layered group space-time signals. Also, to mitigate the performance loss resulting from the group processing, the proposed MUD makes use of the PSI fed back from the previous group to detect the symbols in each group. Simulation results demonstrate that the new MUD can offer a substantial performance gain over pervious works.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of stability in a passively mode-locked fiber laser with polarization effect
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel model describing the operation of a passively mode-locked fiber laser with polarization effect is developed. The combinational effect of the linear gain, nonlinear gain arising from saturable absorption, gain filtering and polarization effect has been investigated. In this paper we analyze the Schroedinger equation with the polarization effect linearly, and obtain the growth rate of the modulational instability, as well as get the relationship between the growth rate and the laser's gain. With regard to CW situation, if the linear gain is below the threshold, then the growth rate is positive and the CW solution becomes unstable; if it is above the threshold, then the rate is negative, suppressing the modulational instability and making CW to stabilize. Therefore, in this way, the mode locking for the optical fiber laser can be realized.

articleTitle: Polarimetric radiometer-retrieved wind direction ambiguity removal using twice-scan schedule
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: We present a method for evaluating characteristics of wind vector retrieval error's from polarimetric radiometer measurements such as WindSat. Focus is put on moving wind direction errors due to ambiguous solutions, with azimuth angle being 0 and 180. We propose a method to obtain wind direction according to first and second rank solutions of the first scan and first rank solution of the second scan. This algorithm can avoid ambiguous solution.

articleTitle: Simulation of Beam-Wave Interaction for Millimeter Wave Coupled-Cavity Traveling Wave Tube Using PIC
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A method of particle-in-cell (PIC) has been introduced to simulate beam-wave interaction of millimeter wave coupled-cavity traveling wave tube (TWT). The principle of PIC was analyzed theoretically. Both the move track of particles of electron beam and the change of electric field were simulated before and after beam-wave interaction with our self-designed PIC software. The simulation results show that dynamic beam-wave interaction of millimeter wave TWT can be expressed accurately using PIC, which may provide guidance for the research of beam-wave interaction of TWT.

articleTitle: Study on Ripple of Output Voltage of Chaotic Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Chaotic spectrum-spread technology is advantageous in improving EMC of power converters, but it increases ripple of output voltage. This paper puts forward a method for calculating output voltage' s ripple of chaotic power converter. Simulation shows, ripple of output voltage increases with the increase of chaotic modulation coefficient. For suppressing the ripple of output voltage, we suggest adding an active filter to the output circuit of power converter, the active filter has small size and low cost, and its effect to the dynamic characteristic of power converter is small.

articleTitle: A Solution of Video Sensor Node Implementation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The video sensor is a new type of sensor node, which could capture and transmit video media. In this paper, three methods are introduced for video sensor node implementation based on the standardized UDP/TCP protocols and WiFi hardware. And the implementation solutions are described in detail.

articleTitle: A Straightforward Design method for the Top-L Coupled Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on the internal couple coefficient, external Q value and impedance matching, a straightforward design technique for top-L coupled bandpass filters has been developed. Computer simulation results prove its availability. The novel design method has provided a greater intuitive understanding of the top-L coupled bandpass filter.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Parallel Interference Cancellation for DS/CDMA Systems over Rayleigh Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper firstly investigates an optimal parallel interference cancellation (PIC) scheme for an asynchronous DS/CDMA system. Secondly, to reduce the high implementation complexity encountered by the optimal PIC, we propose a low-complexity PIC by simplifying decision complexity and taking weight of the estimated multi-access interference for each interference cancellation (IC) stage. The performance of the low-complexity PIC over Rayleigh fading channel is analyzed and compared to the optimal PIC and conventional PIC, respectively. The simulation results show that the low-complexity PIC, whether IC weight coefficients are taken or not, shows a performance comparable to the optimal PIC and dominantly outperforms the conventional PIC. It is also shown that the low-complexity PIC with two IC stages is superior to the conventional PIC with three IC stages in performance, which is of practical value because PIC with fewer stages can bring shorter processing delay.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis for Vector Quantization of Distributed Source
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The complexity of vector quantization increase exponentially with the vector dimension limits the dimension that can be used in quantizer. But the quantitative relation of performance and complexity isn't clear for quantization of distributed source. In this paper, the rate and distortion of distributed source vector quantization are characterized and analyzed through the point density function of a quantizer. The function of rate, distortion and dimension is then derived. Moreover, the asymptotically performance of vector quantization are analyzed. Simulation results show that vector quantization of distributed source can approach Wyner-Ziv bound in the lower dimension case.

articleTitle: Two-double Post Waveguide BPF on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a 4.7 GHz Multilayered Substrate Integrated Waveguide (MSIW) bandpass filter based on PCB or LTCC is presented. The filter consists of one MSIW cavities in a multilayer design, with a coupling circular-post, and a slot aperture. It is found that the filter can deliver a simulated bandwidth of 100 MHz, centered at 4.67 GHz with an insertion loss of 1 dB, and a pole at 4. 48 GHz.

articleTitle: Space-Time Block Codes from Coordinate Symmetric Super-Orthogonal Designs
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we propose space-time block codes from coordinate symmetric super-orthogonal designs. Compared with space time block codes from complex orthogonal designs, our codes can reduce the bit error rate, improve the performance of system, and exist for more transmit antennas.

articleTitle: Threshold voltage model of deep submicrometer double-gate fully-depleted SOI MOS devices
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the threshold voltage model using a quasi-2D approximation for deep submicrometer double-gate fully-depleted SOI PMOS devices was described by solving basic semiconductor physical equations. Taking into consideration the distribution of minority carriers in the silicon film, the analytical threshold voltage model to make an accurate prediction of short-channel effect has been obtained, and also a further threshold voltage model including DIBL effect and interface charge effect was obtained. The analytical voltage model applies also to SOI NMOS devices. All of the above models have been verified by the results of 2D device simulator MEDICI.

articleTitle: Comprehension of Designing Multi-frequency and multi-polarization Stacked-patch Antenna of Low-AR and High-Gain at Large Theta Angle
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A kind of probe-group-fed multi-layer right-hand-circular polarized (RHCP) and left-hand-circular polarized (LHCP) antenna is discussed in this paper. The basic theory on BW(bandwidth),AR(axial ratio), Gain and some methods for optimization BW, AR, Gain have been given. The conclusion has been pointed out for designing antennas of low-AR and high-Gain in large theta angles for GPS communication system.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization Design of High Order Mode Rectangular Cavities
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a design procedure of a high order mode rectangular cavity is proposed, where a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">315</sub> mode rectangular resonant cavity is chosen as an example for describing the design process. Then the design optimization method is put forward and applied to design a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">315</sub> rectangular cavity operated at 5.8 GHz frequency band. The resonant mode analysis of the rectangular cavity has been presented. The measurement results of the cavity demonstrate the effectiveness of this design procedure.

articleTitle: The Presence and Future of Information Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper analyzes the research background of present-day information network and technologies firstly. And then we introduce the main work and some achievements in BJTU NGIRC in recent years. We also introduce the future research work in BJTU NGIRC.

articleTitle: Relay Region Analysis for Amplify-and-Forward Cooperative Communications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Cooperative network with the amplify-and-forward (AF) protocol is attractive for its simplicity and nonloss of soft information. In this paper, we analyze relay region where cooperative transmission with the AF protocol outperforms direct transmission. In high SNR regimes, we derive an analytical expression of the relay region, and propose a geometric explanation for uncoded binary phase shift keying (BPSK) modulation. Simulation results confirm our theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Bandstop Filter Base on Composite right/left-handed (CRLH) Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel bandstop filter based on composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line (TL) is proposed and studied. This designed bandstop filter provides low passband insertion loss, very sharp transitions at the edges of the stopband, large attenuation in the stopband, easy fabrication, and low cost. The performances of the proposed filter are demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Conduction EMI in Substation and Design of Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: EMI caused by switching operations is measured practically in a few substations. Conduction harassment property is analyzed in substation secondary systems or low-voltage AC power systems. Its characteristics in time and frequency domain are given. To counter these characteristics, frequency properties of insertion losses and property impedances of a few reality power filters are studied. An experimental filtering circuit is designed and its filtering effects on electrical fast transience/burst and oscillatory waves are both tested. Requirements of filtering property of substation power filter are defined.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Propagation of High Power Microwave in Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Considering electron temperature arising time, new concepts of safe pulse length threshold and safe amplitude threshold are put forward. Combined with electron kinetic equation, electron energy equation and Maxwell equations, a FDTD method is proposed to analyze the nonlinear propagation characteristics of high power microwave in lower ionosphere. And also, the relationship of safe pulse length threshold, safe amplitude threshold with frequency, electron number density and collision frequency are discussed.

articleTitle: Capacity Evaluation of Cellular TDD-CDMA Systems Deploying Multi-frequency
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Both uplink and downlink capacity of cellular time duplex division-code division multiple access (TDD-CDMA) systems deploying multi-frequency are analyzed theoretically. The impact of multi-user detection, inter-frequency interference and different traffic types on multi-frequency TDD-CDMA system capacity are discussed. Simulation is done to evaluate the theoretical analysis and a good concordance is observed. Simulation and theoretical results show that adjacent channel leakage ratio should at least 10 dB to achieve higher capacity by deploying multi-frequency. When adjacent channel leakage ratio is bigger than 30 dB, the capacity of N frequency system is exact N times that of single frequency system. The conclusions are true for both uplink and downlink.

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: Conformal Low-profile E-shaped Patch Antenna with Unequal Thickness Substrate
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A conformal low-profile e-shaped patch antenna is presented in this paper. Unequal thickness substrate is used in the patch antenna design to maintain the wide-band characteristic of the conformal e-shaped patch antenna. Conformal patch antennas with unequal thickness substrate are fabricated and measured. The experimental results show that the patch antennas provide stable return loss and radiation patterns with different curvature. The result is useful for the design of conformal antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Analysis of ohmic quality factor for the Azimuthally Symmetrical TE03-mode 42GHz gyrotron cavity
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A simple electromagnetic method has been presented, by dividing the input- and output- taper sections of cavity into numbers of non-tapered circular steps, to calculate the ohmic quality factor of tapered cavity of a 42 GHz, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub>-mode gyrotron. The energy stored in cavity and power loss on cavity-wall, have been estimated in sinusoidal field profile. For the typically chosen non-tapered cavity, the calculated value of ohmic quality factor, in the present paper, was found within 4% of the results calculated using two of previously published expressions. The validation/ comparison of results against simulation software: MAGIC have been made and found within 3%. Further, the effect of structure dimensions, namely, length of mid-section of the cavity, input-taper angle and output-taper angle, on value of the ohmic quality factor for a tapered gyrotron cavity have been studied. It is found that the ohmic quality factor for a tapered gyrotron cavity, other parameters remaining constant, increases with decrease of length of mid-section and input-taper angle, and with increase of output-taper angle. Out of input- and output-taper angles, the latter was found more sensitive controlling parameter for the ohmic quality factor and hence frequency selectivity as well as ohmic heating in a tapered cavity. Furthermore, the contours of length of mid-section and ohmic quality factor were plotted to provide flexibility to the designer in optimising the structure parameters of tapered cavity of a 42 GHz, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub>-mode gyrotron.

articleTitle: Application of Parallel Genetic Algorithm with Two-step Fitness Function forthe design of Multi-band Single-Layer Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The parallel genetic algorithm (PGA) with two-step fitness function is proposed to design the multi-band single-layer frequency selective surface (FSS). The inner-outer flexible generalized minimal residual algorithm combined with fast Fourier transform (FGMRES-FFT) method is used to accelerate the convergence of the system equation of method of moment. An example of the tri-band single-layer FSS structure is given to demonstrate the validity of the present method.

articleTitle: Image reconstruction of uiform circular array synthetic aperture radiometer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Bright temperature image reconstruction of synthetic aperture radiometer (SAIR) with uniform circular array (UCA) is studied. After analysis of baseline patter of UCA, an reconstruction algorithm using discrete fourier transform (DFT) and generalized inverse matrix method both is presented. The theoretic highest space resolution of UCA SAIR is analyzed based on derivation of the algorithm. An expression of the optimal normalized radius of UCA and estimation of corresponding radial resolution are presented. The computer simulation results are given out to validate this method. Superresolution capability of the algorithm is shown also.

articleTitle: Location Determination with Four Elements Antenna Using Matrix Pencil Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A 3D location determination method using only four elements antenna is proposed. A group of frequencies is received from the transmitter (on mobile phone) or returned signals (Radar). The matrix pencil method is used to identify the length of each path. Depending on the geometrical distribution of the four elements, the phase shifts are determined for each path. Knowing the phase shift between the elements helps to find the direction of arrival for each path. Small dipole or small circular loop antennas are used in the numerical examples to clarify this method in the presence of noise.

articleTitle: A Technique for Eureka-147 Digital Audio Broadcasting Fine Symbol Timing Offset Estimation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a new algorithm in Ereka-147 digital audio broadcasting (DAB) symbol timing offset estimation. The proposed algorithm performs robust operation and low complication in symbol timing offset estimation. The performance of this algorithm is carried out under AWGN and multipath fading channel.

articleTitle: Application of Photonic Crystals in sub-terahertz-wave Switch
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel compact sub-terahertz wave switch based on photonic crystals is proposed. We have investigated the performance of the proposed sub-terahertz wave switch by using plane wave expansion and finite-difference time-domain method. The numerical results show that an excellent sub-terahertz wave switch at a frequency of 0.1THz is achieved. The proposed sub-terahertz wave switch has a high extinction ratio of -40dB, and small size of 6.811mm. It has a potential application to sub-terahertz wave communication systems.

articleTitle: Complex Rays Expansion of Three Dimension Radiation Pattern Using Buckyball Grid
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The method of complex rays expansion of three dimensions radiation pattern is proposed basing on the Gauss characteristic of the paraxial far fields from complex source. The Gauss beams shooting from the origin to the gird nodes of the Buckyball distribute uniformly in all directions. The effect of the parameters of beam width and discrete interval to the simulation of pattern are analyzed, and the experiential choices of the parameters are given. The simulative results show a high simulative precision.

articleTitle: The Solution to Array Signal Ambiguity Base on High Order Cumulate
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: On the arrary signal processing, the problem of signal ambiguity exists because that the minimum of the space between elements is larger than half of the wavelength. Baseing on discussing how the signal ambiguity exists and the principium of array augmentation with high-order cumulate, a high-order cumulate algorithm to resolve the the signal ambiguity problem is studied in this paper, which is utilizeing the characteristic of array augmentation with high-order cumulate.

articleTitle: Relationship between Satellite Attitude Jitter and ScanSAR Mosaic
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Attitude stability is a very important parameter for the platform design of scanning synthetic aperture radar (ScanSAR) satellite. In this paper, the effect of satellite attitude jitter on spaceborne ScanSAR mosaic in range is analyzed in detail based on a mathematical model describing satellite attitude jitter, to provide a theoretical guideline for the design of spaceborne ScanSAR system, as verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive QoS Management for Delivering Scalable Video over OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive QoS management framework for delivering scalable video over OFDM system.The proposed framework has two advantages: One is to admit as many base layer video streams as possible while meeting the hard guarantees for all base layer video streams, the other is to adapt the enhancement layer video streams based on the available residual resources to provide the same quality improvement among the admitted users. Simulated results show that the system resources are shared in a fair manner while perceptual quality is degraded gracefully under severe channel conditions and new call.

articleTitle: Determination of the Phase Noise Sources of CMOS-Integrated LC Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The classical Floquet perturbation theory can not provide a deeper observation on the phase noise of oscillation excited by the complicated noise source, and are limited to a particular circuit and the assumption of stationary noise sources. In this paper, the key steps for the novel technique based on the stochastic differential equations are studied to capture the noise-energy contribution of the interesting nodes in the circuits to the overall PSD. The numerical results illustrate the practicability of the presented method as expected by showing the quantitative analysis and comparison of contributors of phase noise between the standard LC oscillator and that in SOC.

articleTitle: A New Transmission Scheme for Railway Based on OFDM-SFN
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new transmission scheme for railway wireless communication. By realizing single frequency network based on OFDM, we improved the performance of GSM-R by realizing "soft handover" . And in order to improve our system' s performance in frequency selective multipath channel, we adopt generalized Multi-Carrier-CDMA (GMC-CDMA) scheme to optimize our system. Relying on symbol blocking and judicious design of user' s code, GMC CDMA could obtain a better interference resilient performance in multipath fading channel while guaranteeing a good symbol recovery.

articleTitle: Diffraction Tomography Algorithm for Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A fast diffraction tomography algorithm for ground penetrating radar is derived in this paper. The algorithm uses the first born approximation and the dyadic Green's function for a two layer medium to get a linear forward model that takes into account the planar air-soil interface. The forward model is then inverted using Fourier transform and this can be implemented with FFT, so the algorithm can reconstruct object rapidly. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate performance of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Guided Modes in a Slab Waveguide of Anisotropic dispersive Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: We derive the guidance conditions of a slab waveguide of uniaxially anisotropic dispersive material with not all of the components in the permittivity and permeability tensor the same sign. Taking the lossless dispersive left-handed media model for example, in terms of the operating angular frequency ω0 of the metamaterial, the even mode properties for guided TE waves are discussed in three classes. When ω2 mpz<ω20<ω2mp⊥ there are infinite guided modes. In addition, it is also found that there may be multiple solutions of the propagating mode with wave number when imaginary transverse wave number ω2em<ω20<ω2mpz.

articleTitle: A New Low-Frequency Model of Absorber Array Founded by Transmission/Reflection Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to predict performance of anechoic chamber with absorbers by simulation, an equivalent layer model of absorbing array should be needed, which can be carried out by homogenization. In this procedure, absorbing array is replaced by a uniform media with a effective electromagnetic properties in transverse direction, and divided a proper number of layers in longitudinal direction. In order to obtain the effective properties of each layer, a two-port network model of period cell based on transmission/reflection method (NRW)[3][6][7] will be founded. We will calculate effective properties through the scattering parameters on two ports, and then substitute each group of properties into corresponding layer model to get reflectivity. According to comparing the reflectivity among the model founded by NRW, the model by Hasin-shtrikman (HS) bound and the model of initial pyramid array, it can be proved that the method in this paper can get a better approximating result especially in low-frequency range (below 100 MHz).

articleTitle: Research on satellite-to-ground optical communication and AO technique
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In satellite-to-ground optical communication, the effect of atmosphere turbulence to communication system is a very important problem. The effect of laser beam propagating in the turbulent atmosphere and the performance of communication system are analyzed in this paper. Adaptive optics (AO) technique can be used to solve this problem of turbulent atmosphere. There are emphasis research on the effect of communication link error rate on different turbulence and improvement of performance when using AO technique; the simulation results are presented in paper. AO technique plays an important role in satellite-to-ground laser communication.

articleTitle: Doubly Selective Fading Channel Tracking Based on Particle Filter in MIMO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Time selectivity and frequency selectivity are the main characteristics of wireless communication channels. To track doubly selective fading channels in MIMO-OFDM systems, a novel channel estimation algorithm based on particle filter is proposed. We model the fading channel as an autoregressive (AR) process and encode the transmit signal using space-time block code (STBC) scheme. In the receiver, channel estimation and symbol detection are alternated, and maximum likelihood (ML) scheme is used for symbol detection. Simulation results show that the proposed method has more effective tracking performance than traditional methods based on training symbols and offers much improved spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Based on Manifold Ranking and PCA
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel framework for face recognition based on manifold ranking algorithm and PCA algorithm. First, manifold ranking algorithm is used to explore the relationship among all the data points in the feature space, and then constructs a weighted graph with respect to the intrinsic manifold structure collectively revealed by all the space data. So the images can be measured and ranked respect to the similarity of image data. The front r images of one category in the retrieval result are selected because of no accord between such manifold structure and the semantic concept belong to the same image. Finally, the PCA algorithm is applied to face recognition on the selected images and the sample face image. The experimental results from face images data illustrate the validity of our method.

articleTitle: Initialization Analysis of IIR Ground Clutter Filter in Doppler Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper analyzes the initialization of IIR ground clutter filter (GCF) in Doppler weather radar. The transients of IIR GCF degrade the theoretical frequency response and different initialization technique produces different suppression characteristic. The initialization performance is tested both with a simulated weather radar signal and an actual weather radar signal. We explore the relation between clutter suppression ratio (the power of the unfiltered signals to the power of the filtered signals) and number of samples. Through simulations, the results demonstrate that the suppression characteristic of step-initialized and projection-initialized IIR GCF each has its advantage and you can choose as you need.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on Electromagnetic Scattering of Hypersonic Sphere and Ionized Wake
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents RCS results at X band and Ka waveband radar system of steel sphere models with 10 mm diameter and aluminium sphere models with 10 mm diameter and 15 mm diameter. The model velocities exceed 5 km/s, and the experiment pressure range is 3173 Pa to 11219 Pa. The electromagnetic scattering properties of hypersonic spheres and wakes at X waveband monostatic mode and Ka waveband bistatic mode are obtained. The results present that the RCS of non- ablation sphere models and ablation sphere models is larger than the RCS of their ionized wakes, and the sphere models signals at X waveband radar are easily separated from their ionized wakes, and measured wake signals at X waveband radar are easily distinguished from background.

articleTitle: High-order accurate ADI-FDTD method with high-order spatial accuracy
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new concept of the exponential evolution operator (EEO) is introduced, from which the conventional ADI-FDTD method can be derived. And what's more important, new high-order accurate unconditionally-stable ADI-FDTD method can be constructed from the EEO. In order to improve spatial accuracy, fourth-order accurate central finite difference scheme is used in the new method. The final analysis shows that its numerical dispersion error is greatly reduced in compared with that of the conventional one. In this paper, the principal characteristics and the disadvantages of genetic algorithm and BP algorithm are introduced.

articleTitle: Subcell FDTD for Computing the Cutoff Frequency of the Waveguide Loaded with Electrically Thin Dispersive Layer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel method for computing the cutoff frequency of the waveguide loaded with the electrically thin dispersive layer is introduced. The proposed method is based on the subcell FDTD technique and Z transforms. The most significant feature of the proposed method is its ability to compute the cutoff frequency of the waveguide loaded with rather complicated dispersive layers having multiple pole pairs. The method is validated with several numerical examples making comparison with the exact results. Keywords: Cutoff frequency of the waveguide, Electrically thin dispersive layers, Subcell FDTD, Z Transforms.

articleTitle: Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles: A service replication protocol in mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract:
Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles

"A Service Replication Protocol in Mobile Ad hoc Networks"
by He Linna and Yin Wei
in the Proceedings of the IEEE 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation, and EMC Technologies For Wireless Communications (MAPE 2007)

After careful and considered review of the content and authorship of this paper by a duly constituted expert committee, this paper has been found to be in violation of IEEE's Publication Principles.

This paper contains significant portions of original text from the paper cited below. The original text was copied without attribution (including appropriate references to the original author(s) and/or paper title) and without permission.

Due to the nature of this violation, reasonable effort should be made to remove all past references to this paper, and future references should be made to the following article:

"A Pull-based Service Replication Protocol in Mobile Ad hoc Networks"
by Abdelouahid Derhab and Nadjib Badache
in the European Transactions on Telecommunications, vol 18, issue 1, January 2007


The mobility of nodes in ad hoc networks can lead to frequent network partitioning. This partitioning disconnects many nodes from a centralised server. Being aware of a future partitioning can help to provide a continuous service availability for all mobile nodes. We propose a service replication protocol consisting of three distributed algorithms. This protocol predicts the occurrence of network partitioning, which allows to create service replicas in the future separate partitions. Our simulation results show that the proposed protocol guarantees service availability to all mobile nodes without incurring high cost.

articleTitle: 126 GHz Fully-Balanced Oscillator and 1/4 Dynamic Divider in 0.25μm SiGe:C BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a 126 GHz fully balanced tunable oscillator followed by a 1/4 dynamic divider, designed in a 0.25 μm SiGe:C BiCMOS technology with f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tau</sub>=190 GHz and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>=200 GHz. The simulated oscillating frequency can be tuned from 118 to 126 GHz with an output power of -0. 4 dBm and a phase noise of -98. 7 dBc/Hz at the frequency offset of 10 MHz. A harmonic mixer was also integrated on the same chip for testing the oscillator output.

articleTitle: Effects induced by the third-order dispersion in TPC system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper shows the compensation progress of the second-order dispersion and the self-phase modulation (SPM) in temporal phase conjugation (TPC) system. And it gives a description of oscillations induced by the third-order dispersion. The theoretical analysis and numerical simulations reveal that TPC can only compensate for second-order dispersion and SPM but enhance effects caused by the third-order dispersion.

articleTitle: The Research of High Power Microwave Interaction in Lower Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The propagation of High Power Microwave(HPM) can produce nonlinear effect in lower ionosphere. In this paper, the analytical interaction effect of HPM in lower ionosphere, and the relation of interaction factor with the initial electric field and microwave frequency is analyzed when HPM propagates in lower ionosphere and then simulate numerically the relation and show the figures. The conclusion shows that the value of E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>(0)/E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> should be controlled below the "ten" when HPM propagates in lower ionosphere, to reduce absorption attenuation.

articleTitle: Full-rate and Low Complexity Space-time Coding Scheme Concatenated with LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a full-rate and low complexity space-time coding scheme with complex orthogonal design is developed, and LDPC code is employed as channel coding to improve the proposed scheme performance further. Compared with full-diversity space-time code schemes, the developed scheme can implement full data rate, low calculation complexity and partial diversity; and it can adopt lower order modulation scheme under the same system throughput. Moreover, using the developed scheme can form efficient spatial interleaving, thus the performance loss due to partial diversity is effectively compensated by the concatenation of channel coding. Simulation results show that on the condition of the same system throughput and concatenation of channel coding, the developed scheme has lower bit error rate than those low-rate and full-diversity multiple antennas space-time coding schemes.

articleTitle: A Novel Generic Cross-Layer Architecture for Next Generation Mobile Communication System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The traditional protocol stack cannot adapt to tire dynamic changing wireless environment, which severely limits the performance improvement of the communication system. To cope with this problem, the generic cross-layer architecture (GCLA) is proposed in this paper and a cross-layer algorithm is also introduced in details based on GCLA. The analysis shows that GCLA outperforms the Client-Server architecture in correctness, maintainability, and execution efficiency, which will ease the future work on both the cross-layer architecture design and the implementation of cross-layer algorithms.

articleTitle: Novel Circularly Polarized Square Microstrip Antenna with L-Slits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel microstrip antenna with four L-slits for achieving circular polarization (CP) operation is proposed. By introducing two pairs of the centrosymmetric L-slits, the high cross-polar level is effectively suppressed. The characteristics of the input impedance, axial ratio, and radiation patterns are simulated. The results show that the good CP performance of the proposed antenna can be obtained.

articleTitle: Pencil beam pattern synthesis using perturbation technique and fast Fourier transforms
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Using perturbation technique, the linear relation between the array pattern and its parameter (current, spacing) perturbation can be established. In a simple and fast way, the formulas to determine parameter perturbations by FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) algorithms are developed and presented in this paper. These formulas can be generically applied in the array synthesis to approach the specified pattern or to improve the pattern performance. Applying them on the synthesis of pencil beam patterns, for which the lower sidelobe levels and/or narrower main beam width are desired, it is shown that the sidelobe reduction can be easily achieved, meanwhile keeping a desired narrow beam width.

articleTitle: Efficient Consistency Control for Mobile Dynamic Contents Delivery Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper is to design an integrated consistency-control algorithm for mobile contents delivery network (M-CDN) to enhance the efficient utilization of network resource and support the client mobility. Firstly, by carrying out an analysis of mobile surrogates characteristics, for a given content which has been changed on its original node, only a limited number of its replicas instead of all replicas are updated. Then, if a replica has been selected for update, the latest version will be sent from an algorithm-decided site instead of from its original server.

articleTitle: Analysis of Radiating Electric Field for Indoor Broadband Power Line Communication
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Broadband power line communication (BPL) is a novel technology for constructing home networks. However, the electric field radiating from the power lines could change the indoor electromagnetic environment even disturb other radio communication services. Thus, a model based on four- port networks is proposed to evaluate the radiating field. Numerous branches of power lines are also taken into account. The radiating electric field from a 12-m-long indoor power line with 3 branches has been measured and the results demonstrate the practical value of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Based Blind Beamforming for Multiusers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a new genetic algorithm (GA) based blind beamforrming algorithm for multiusers without the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization (GSO). This algorithm can estimate weight vectors by defining a new cost function based on the kurtosis maximization algorithm (KMA) and the cross-correlation of the beamformer port outputs. Moreover, to overcome the local optimal problem existing in the stochastic gradient algorithms, a global optimal solution of nonlinear weighting vector estimation is obtained by complex coding genetic algorithm (CC-GA) proposed in this paper. The coded parameters in the CC-GA are composed of real parts and imaginary parts of complex weight vectors. The fitness function equivalent to the objective function of the traditional optimization techniques is constructed by the new cost function. The performance of the new algorithm is analyzed with computer simulation.

articleTitle: A New Methodology Protect Smart Cards from DPA
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Since power analysis on smart cards was introduced by Paul Kocher, many countermeasures have been proposed to protect implementations of cryptographic algorithms. In this paper many countermeasures are being discussed, point out unique masking method can not protect from higher-order differential power analysis. We proposed a new protection method. It uses coupled circuit structure for a DES circuit. The theory of UMM and experiments shows its efficiency.

articleTitle: Research of Power Density Standard from 1GHz to 18GHz
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper is aim to establish a precise microwave power density standard device, whose frequency range is from 1GHz to 18GHz and the maximum value can be 10mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It can satisfy the requirements of the calibration of microwave probe better and solve the problem of affiliation for microwave power density.

articleTitle: Crosstalk on Sampling Clock and Additive Dither in Radio Receiver IF Digitization
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Radio receiver intermediate frequency digitization generally requires high resolution of analog-to-digital conversion with wide bandwidth. The sampling clock performance is a key concern and is widely investigated in the published literatures. However, most of the issues mainly focused on the clock jitter with white Gaussian noise only. This paper present a more realistic analog-to-digital conversion analysis model based on the actual circuit noise conditions, particularly investigating on the clock jitter error with the combination of Gauss distribution noise and circuit noise (interference). An analytical expression for the A/D conversion with the combined clock jitter error is developed. The computer simulations are presented, which showed excellent agreement with the developed expression. Also, a solution of additive dithering technique is present to reduce the effect of circuit crosstalk on sampling clock.

articleTitle: An approach to designing linear array with high accuracy in direction of arrival estimation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper we analyzed the relationship between the accuracy of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation and manifold length of linear array, abstracted from it an index to compare the accuracy of DOA estimation among linear arrays. Based on analysis of the index, an approach to design linear array with high accuracy in DOA estimation was presented. The results of stimulation verify the effectiveness of the index and the approach.

articleTitle: A Fast Solution to the Volume Integral Equation for 3-D Dielectric Objects by Using the Precorrected-FFT with Floating Stencil
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A fast solution to the volume integral equation (VIE) for 3-D dielectric objects is implemented by using the precorrected-FFT method with floating stencil topology. The object is discretized into tetrahedral volume elements and is modeled by SWG basis functions. When the P-FFT method is being carried out, the projection and interpolation stencils are based on a new stencil topology named " floating stencil" , in which each grid corresponds to a stencil center and only the basis functions around one stencil's center are linked to that stencil. Numerical results show that the floating stencils can significantly reduced near-zone interactions to be pre-corrected, as well as memory and CPU time.

articleTitle: Improved Joint Data and Channel Estimation for OFDM Systems Using Few Symbols
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Literature [1] proposed new blind joint data and channel estimator solved by Sphere Decoding algorithm. In this paper, based on this new estimator we propose two modified blind joint estimators. Both of them extend the number of employed OFDM symbols from one to a limited quantity. The first modified estimator, as the original one, assumes that the channel impulse response (CIR) is constant in one OFDM symbol and could vary between symbols, while the second assumes that the CIR is constant in a limited number of symbols. Simulations show that our modified estimators perform better than the original one.

articleTitle: Novel Blind Decision Feedback Equalization Algorithm for Wireless Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In wireless communications, blind equalization plays an important role in combating inter-symbol interference (ISI) introduced by multipath fading wireless channels, and its main performance criterions are residual mean square error (MSE), convergence speed, and complexity. In this paper, an efficient blind decision feedback equalization algorithm suitable for wireless communication channels is proposed. The performance of the new method is compared to traditional blind decision feedback algorithm by means of computer simulations, and the simulation results confirm the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: LU Decomposition Method in Calculating Electric Field Components of 2-D ADI-FDTD
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The alternating-direction implicit-finite-difference time-domain (ADI-FDTD) method is unconditionally stable. The method should solve systems of linear equations in calculating electric field components of 2-D ADI-FDTD. For the coefficient matrixes of the systems are 3-diagonal strip matrixes, this paper adopts LU decomposition method to solve the systems. The efficiency can be improved above 50%. And the validity and rapidity are verified through an example of 2-D TM wave propagating in vacuum.

articleTitle: QR-AMCBFM for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An adaptively modified characteristic basis function method (AMCBFM) with QR factorization based on a dual modified Gram-Schmidt (Dual-MGS) algorithm called QR-AMCBFM is presented. Primary basis functions was derived by AMCBPM. When higher level basis functions are calculated, the QR factorization algorithm with Dual-MGS is used to decompose mutual coupling matrixes. The factorization scheme will stop by employing different threshold values set in near and far field domains. And the rest interaction between farther blocks will be ignored. Once the' adjacent currents precision arrives at a certain criterion, the higher-level basis functions would not be necessary, in which entire process the algorithm estimates adaptively. The numerical results show that the QR-AMCBFM can solve real problems accurately and can save more RAM storage and CPU time than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Equalization with Ordered PIC for Single Carrier MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Single carrier (SC) multiple input multiple output (MIMO) system with frequency domain equalization (FDE) is regarded as one of the best candidates for uplink broadband wireless communication systems. This paper proposes a FDE with ordered parallel interference cancellation (FDE-OPIC) for uplink SOMIMO system. Due to the gain brought by the ordering and Gauss-Seidel iteration, the proposed FDE-OPIC outperforms FDE with parallel interference cancellation (FDE-PIC) by about 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">~</sup>2 dB when target BER equals 10E-3. Besides, FDE-OPIC with 2 iterations can even achieve the same performance as FDE with ordered successive interference cancellation (FDE-OSIC) while still holding low complexity in severe frequency selective channel.

articleTitle: Investigation of Mutual Coupling Effect on the Interference Rejection Capability of Linear Patch Array in CDMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The suitable use of an array antenna at the base station of a wireless communication system can result in improvement in signal-to-interference ratio (SIR). In general, the SIR is a function of the direction of arrival of the desired signal and depends on the configuration of the array, the number of elements, and their spacing. The performance criteria for SIR improvement employed in this paper is the spatial interference suppression coefficient. In this paper, we consider uniform linear array of circular patch antenna and study the effect of varying the number of elements on the SIR performance. We quantitatively assess the degradation in SIR performance as we move from broadside to end-fire direction. In addition, the effect of mutual coupling (MC) is taken into account.

articleTitle: Effect of pH Value on Microstructure and Magnetic properties of NiZn ferrite thin films
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: NiZn ferrite thin films were performed on glass substrates of 85°C by spin spray plating method. X-ray diffraction patterns of the films show that the samples have a cubic spinel structure between 75°C and 85°C. As the pH value of oxidizing solution increases to 8.3, the saturation magnetization increases to 313emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and resistivity to 1.27 Ω • cm. Film deposited at pH 7.8 has a smooth surface and definite columnar structure. The large wavy flakes were observed at pH 8. 3. The high real part of complex permeability μ' up to 36. 1 and the imaginary part μ" up to 53. 2 were observed at 0.5GHz by shorted microstrip line perturbation method. The μ" of thin film has values higher than 20 at the frequencies between 0.5GHz and 2GHz, the film is a promising shielding material for high frequency applications.

articleTitle: A Novel LFMCW Scheme of the Real-Time Tracking the DDS by the PLL
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, two schemes of traditional linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) source are analyzed. Based on the analysis, a novel LFMCW scheme of the real-time tracking the direct digital frequency synthesis (DDS) by the phase locked loop (PLL) is proposed. The frequency of the LFMCW source's output signal ranges from 1.5 GHz to 1.8 GHz. Compared with traditional schemes, the new scheme is characterized by the following features: high linearity, high stability, immune to environmental influence, good spur suppression and low phase noise, etc.

articleTitle: Blind Decoding Algorithm in Vertical Layered MultiCarrier System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A rotation invariant property is deduced in the multicarrier vertical Bell labs layered space-time system (MC V-BLAST) by introducing some redundancy in the transmitter. A direct decoding algorithm using the direction of arrival (DOA) matrix method is proposed to directly detect the original transmitted symbol without knowing channels state information (CSI). This method does not require the number of receive antennas is more than that of the transmit ones. Simulation results demonstrate that this algorithm improves the BER performance 5-7 dB when BER is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>.

articleTitle: The Research of a L Band Low Noise Cryogenic Amplifier Basing on PHEMT
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a L-band low noise cryogenic amplifier using PHEMT is reported. The cryogenic performance of PHEMT and the stability of the circuit are discussed. The design, and experimental results are also presented. At liquid nitrogen temperature, in the frequency of band range from 1.7GHz to 1.9GHz, the cryogenic LNA can achieve following performance : gain more then 21dB, gain plainness less then 1dB, noise figure less then 0.3dB, the input VSWR1 less then 1.3 and the output VSWR2 less then 1.3.

articleTitle: Power Supply Noise Analysis in DSM Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The continuous technology advance into the VDSM regime has brought the noise and signal integrity issues into the spotlight. It seems to be more important to estimate the power supply noise efficiently and accurately than other design metrics such as area, timing and power. At the same time, the capacitive and inductive effect should no longer be ignored in the noise analysis process. In the work, a GA-based statistical modeling technique is presented to find the worst-case time-domain voltage variation in VLSI power distribution network including inductive and resistive effects. And, the statistical power supply noise is also mapped into perturbation of the macroblock delay. Experimental results are put together with SPICE simulations, and show the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Improvement of a Planar Inverted F-Antenna by Introducing Multiple Ground Pins
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A broadband/multi-band planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is presented for wireless communication systems. The bandwidth of the proposed antenna is significantly improved by introducing multiple ground pins. Measured at 10 dB return loss, the operation bands efficiently cover the lower bands from 1.67 to 2.34 GHz for DCS1800/1900, DECT and UMTS, as well as the upper band from 4.8 GHz to 5.02 GHz for WLAN applications at. TERR 802.11 j. Excellent impedance matching is achieved across the bandwidth. Measured input impedance, simulated radiation patterns, and gains are presented.

articleTitle: The Decrease of the Radar Cross Section of Hypersonic Model
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: To research the effect of plasma, the radar cross section (RCS) of a hypersonic model is measured in our light gas gun. The spectrum of the received signal and one-dimensional radar image of the model are given. According to this experiment, three-dimensional (3-D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations are performed for calculating microwave scattering from a plasma-cloaked conducting model.

articleTitle: A Novel Six Bit Phase Shifter for the Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel 15-GHz six-bit digital phase shifter has been proposed. The developed phase shifter has been realized in a hybrid MIC technique with PIN diodes as switching elements. The circuit consists of four bits realized as periodically loaded-line and two bits based on novel switched-line with loaded-line. All of six bits have special tuning elements for the fine tuning of the required phase shift. The insertion loss for the 64 phase states is 5.2dBplusmn1.1 dB over the operating bandwidth of 14.9-15.1GHz, and the phase error for the 64 phase states is not greater than 3.4 degrees at the designed center frequency of 15GHz.

articleTitle: Using Support Vector Machine Regression for Measuring Electromagnetic Parameters of Magnetic Materials
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new method is proposed for electromagnetic parameters (permittivity and permeability) measurement. The microstrip transmission-line is used as measure structure, and supported vector machine (SVM) is introduced to extract actual permittivity and permeability of magnetic materials. Experiment results show that both permittivity and permeability of magnetic materials can be extracted accurately.

articleTitle: Improvement of TCP Congestion Control Algorithm in Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on TCP congestion control algorithm, a new TCP-mobile algorithm is presented and simulated in mobile ad hoc networks. TCP-mobile algorithm is composed of four stages algorithms: the s low start, the congestion avoiding, the fast re-transmit and the fast restoration. But the symbols that this algorithm distinguishes from other algorithms lies in: TCP-mobile algorithm can heuristic differentiate between bit error and network congestion. Simulation results show that, TCP-mobile algorithm can get better performance than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-Destination Multicast Routing Protocol in MANET
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Aiming at a short-term information distribution model a multi-destination multicast routing protocol was presented. It made use of unicast routing information to realize multicast transmission. The intermediate node forwarded multicast packets for the relative destinations according to the destination field and its own routing table. It needed no maintenance of the multicast tree and multicast group. Under this application model, the protocol has comparative packet delivery rate with unicast routing protocols, less transmission overhead and less control bit overhead than the unicast and the other multicast routing protocol.

articleTitle: A Planar Integrated Left-Handed Microstrip Line Formed by Linearly Placed Spiral Elements
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A planar integrated left-handed microstrip line formed by linearly placed spiral elements is presented in this paper. This structure is simple to fabricate and is scalable to higher frequencies, which is ideal for microwave and millimeter-wave hybrid integrated circuit (HMIC) and monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) applications. Left-handed propagations over this kind of transmission line are validated by both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Electric Field and Characteristic Impedance In ATEM Cell With Rectangular Metallic EUT
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: ATEM cell is widely used in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) test. When loaded with equipment under test (EUT), the electric field in ATEM cell will be distorted , and the characteristic impedance changed. In this paper, the field distribution and characteristic impedance in ATEM cell loaded with rectangular metallic EUT is analyzed by a simple method----point matching method. The section of an asymmetric TEM was divided into five regions and potential function is expressed as a Fourier series in each region. The point-matching was used on the interface of these regions to determine coefficients of series. Thus, the characteristic impedance can be calculated and electric field obtained in terms of a potential function.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband propagation channels and their impact on system design
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The performance of ultrawideband (UWB) communications systems is determined by the propagation channels they operate in. This paper gives an overview of UWB channels and their impact on system design. The emphasis lies on (i) multiple-antenna systems and (ii) body-area networks. We discuss the frequency dependence of angular power spectra and show that spatial multiplexing can be used for achieving very high data rates in MIMO-UWB systems. For body-area networks, we And small delay spreads, so that high-rate communications can be supported with relatively simple receiver structures. Finally, we argue that the clustering structure and "soft onset" property of UWB power delay profiles strongly influence the design of ranging systems.

articleTitle: Design of Transceiver for TETRA in UHF Band
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: RF transceiver for TETRA mobile in 800MHz UHF band was designed and fabricated. The essential elements of transceiver such as CFL ASIC, Tx/Rx PLL modules are also designed and fabricated. Using CFL ASIC, more than 20dB of IMD improvement was acquired. To accept the two mode of TETRA(TMO & DMO), two independent PLL modules were used. The output power of transmitter was 0.5W, the specification of EVM and ACP was satisfied with TETRA standard and the dynamic range of receiver was more than 60dB.

articleTitle: Calculation and Experimental Validation of 3-D Parallel Plate Sensor for Transient Electric Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A three-dimensional (3-D) sensor is proposed for transient electric field measurements in this paper. Three direction components of total fields can be measured simultaneously by using 3-D sensor. The 3-D antenna can convert fields to induced voltages, and the optical transmitter can transform electricity signals to light signals. In order to validate the antenna' s configuration, numerical simulation is implemented for calculating models by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, and then several circumstances, for instance, Interelectrode coupling of the 3-D antenna and synthesis of 3-D field and frequency response of the antenna, are analyzed. Based on the results of simulation, a 3-D electric field sensor has been developed. Fiber measurement system with 3-D sensor is calibrated and then is used for transient electric field measurement. The results of measurement show that wide frequency response of this sensor agrees with the requirements of transient electromagnetic field measurement.

articleTitle: Radar Target's Angular Glint Based on the RCS
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A method of analyzing and calculating the angular glint of complex targets is presented. By dividing the target into very small size cells, and using high-frequency approximation, the Radar Cross Section (RCS) is calculated based on the SCTE prediction system. The angular glint is then calculated by the phase gradient. The results show that the angular glint can be calculated exactly and efficiently in the SCTE system.

articleTitle: A Kind of Preconditioners Based on Shifted Operators to Solve Three-Dimensional TVFEM Equations
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the tangential vector finite element method is used for solving the 3D time-harmonic electromagnetic problems. The preconditioned conjugate gradient solver is applied to solve the large sparse indefinite FEM equations. An efficient and robust preconditioner is introduced. The preconditioner is derived from the IC factorization based on shifted Laplace operators. The efficiency of the proposed approach is studied on several numerical model problems. Our numerical results demonstrate that this method is especially effective when TVFEM is applied to solve large-scale time harmonic electromagnetic field problems.

articleTitle: Cross-Layer Relay Selection in Two-hop Cellular Relaying Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper addressing a relay selection scheme in two-hop cellular relaying networks. An optimization problem based on the relay station (RS) selection is proposed to achieve the maximum network throughput. To satisfy the more rigorous quality-of-service (QoS) demand, both the Signal-to-Noise-Rate (SNR) and scheduling delay are considered with the cross-layer design idea. Considering the effect of lower layers, our proposed RS selection algorithm can obtain a good bandwidth and delay performance. Moreover, with the directional antenna, the network throughput can be enhanced greatly. Simulation results show our proposed relay node selection algorithm is efficient and valuable.

articleTitle: Study on Natural Frequencies Tuning Method of Nearest-Neighbor Coupled Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: According to the phase dynamics and desired phase gradient in the nearest-neighbor coupled oscillator array, conditions that the natural frequencies of oscillator elements should be satisfied are gotten in the article. From the conditions we must tune natural frequency of the first element lower and tune natural frequency of the last element higher, if the desired phase gradient of the linear array is positive.
