But an opposite conclusion can be got according to corresponding consequence of other several articles. Rightness of our conclusion can be proved by simulations and experiments. So conditions that the oscillator elements' natural frequencies should satisfied for desired phase gradient in our article is right.

articleTitle: Improve the Effectiveness of Wireless Image Transmission Using Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Data compression method has been a hot issue in the field of image processing. This paper presents the improvement of the effectiveness of image compression by using wavelet transform technology instead of the discrete cosine transform(DCT) technology which has been adopted by MPEG as image compression standard. A set of wireless video surveillance system which has been developed on base of the theory studied in this paper validate the theory.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Anti Noise FM Jamming of Pseudo-random Code Binary Phase Modulation Fuze Based on Doppler Effect
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Performance analysis of the pseudo-random code binary phase modulated (PRC-BPM) fuze is analyzed in this thesis. Firstly, its principle is introduced in brief. On this basis, the signal to jamming ratio (SJR) gain of its receiver in noise FM jamming is deduced in detail with Doppler frequency. Then, the effect of Doppler frequency, pseudo-random code width, the of period pseudo-random code serial and aiming frequency deviation on its performance of anti noise FM jamming is analyzed. The results indicate that the PRC-BPM fuze has better performance of anti noise FM jamming.

articleTitle: A High Resolution Spatial Smoothing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A high resolution spatial smoothing algorithm which takes cross correlation to the autocorrelation matrixes of subarray output is proposed to increase the angular resolution of conventional spatial smoothing techniques. The formula for the algorithm is derived, and the performance of the algorithm is also analyzed. Simulation results demonstrate that the improved algorithm possesses a better resolving ability and a lower SNR threshold than the conventional spatial smoothing technique and the subarray cross correlation spatial smoothing technique for DOA estimation of coherent signals.

articleTitle: Research on Tracking Arithmetic of Six-stance Electromagnetic Sensitivity Position System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: According to the theory of six-stance electromagnetic sensitivity position system, a new tracking arithmetic is advanced to calculate the attitude and position parameters in this paper. The tracking arithmetic uses previous parameters to calculate current parameters and take two kinds of reference to reduce the complex of arithmetic. It improves the calculation efficiency and position precision of this system. It realizes the full-scope sensitivity position. These advantages improve the application of this system in many aspects.

articleTitle: An Improved Routing Protocol in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel routing protocol is proposed to improve the performance of destination-sequenced distance vector (DSDV) routing protocol in mobile ad hoc networks with high mobility. In the improved routing protocol, dissemination of invalid route information is restricted to local area. Meanwhile, a new route reconstruction scheme is used to create a new loop-free route to destination. Simulation results show that compared with DSDV, it can reduce the number of dropped data packets with little increased overhead in mobile ad hoc networks with high mobility.

articleTitle: Analysis of EMP Propagation in Protection Engineering
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a body of revolution finite difference time domain (BOR-FDTD) is introduced. The propagation of the high power microwave (HPM) and ultra wide band (UWB) electromagnetic pulse in protection engineering is analyzed for the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> modes. Some numerical and experimental results showed good agreement, and valuable conclusions are obtained.

articleTitle: Wireless Charging System Based on Switched Beam Smart Antenna Technique
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a scheme for designing a kind of wireless charging system aimed to provide power transmission for personal mobile devices such as cell phone. This scheme consists of three parts: wireless power transmission design, wireless signal transmission design and charging manage design. A circular array consisting of some antenna elements is employed in the scheme as transmit access of power and signal. In the supposed indoor condition, the transfer efficiency can up to 66%. The charging manage adopt a close-loop optimal charging, charging time can be reduced by 30%, and the battery' s life can be lengthened by 20%.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of the Performance about Wireless Modulation Technologies in the Empty and Straight Mine Laneway
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: After studying the fading situation in mine laneway, this paper finds out the relationship between the bit error rate (BER) of the narrowband and wideband signal and the transmission distance in the empty and straight mine laneway channel, and studies the effect of the empty and straight mine laneway channel on the narrowband and wideband signals at the frequency of 900 MHz, 1800 MHz and 2.4 GHz respectively. By analysis and comparison, it is concluded that comparing with the signal at 900 MHz and 1800 MHz, the signal at 2.4 GHz can cover with wider communication range at low data rate; besides, wideband signal can improve the BER performance and is fitter with communication in mine laneway than narrowband signal.

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency-band Coded Orthogonal UWB Chirp Pulse Design for Cognitive NBI Suppression
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a novel frequency-band coded orthogonal UWB pulse design method based on Chirp signal is presented. The new approach uses the chirp signals located at different frequency-bands to synthesize the orthogonal pulses by coding with Pseudo Noise sequence in frequency domain. The auto-correlation and cross-correlation property of the proposed chirp pulses are better than those of other conventional pulses. Furthermore, the new method also improves the efficiency of the instantaneous spectrum and energy of the transmitting UWB signal. In addition, by the aid of cognitive radio technology to adjust the chirp envelope and the frequency-sweeping range of each chirp subpulse , it can guarantee the transmitting UWB signal to be matched with the different UWB spectrum regulations and coexistence, interference avoidance with other traditional narrow band systems. And simulation result showed that the proposed pulse could reduce the effect of NBI on UWB system with litter complexity.

articleTitle: Application of SEM Technique to Characterization of Breast Tumors
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes an approach for the microwave characterization of breast tumors based on the 2D-FDTD simulation. Tumors and the breast tissue are modeled as dielectric targets and homogeneous dispersive media by Debye model. The CNRs (complex natural resonances) of the tumors, which can be used to characterize the tumors, can be extracted by the Prony' s method directly from the time-domain response from the tumors. The tumor response is obtained by the FDTD simulation. Some comparisons are done with different tumors and different frequencies of input pulse. The results show that this technique has the potential as an assistant tool to characterize the breast tumors in conjunction with other imaging techniques for diagnosis.

articleTitle: Research on One Kind of Improved GPSR Secure Routing Protocol
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The characteristic of wireless sensor networks make their routing protocols be confronted with more security challenges than in the traditional networks. This paper analyses the security problems of GPSR-one common wireless sensor network routing protocol, and presents the distributed group identity validation and the multipath routing as defense measure to provide the GPSR routing security. Finally, it gives the simulation of performance analysis on the improved routing protocol.

articleTitle: A Joint Unitary Precoding and Scheduling Algorithm for MIMO-OFDM System with Limited Feedback
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The capacity of MIMO-OFDM system can be increased substantially through spatial multiplexing with linear unitary precoding technique which requires that full channel state information should be sent back to transmitter. To reduce the feedback overhead, we give a codebook of precoding matrices that is known to both transmitter and receiver. A matrix is selected at the receiver, and then its index is conveyed to the transmitter using a small number of bits. In this work, we propose a new proportional fairness scheduler integrated with unitary precoding for MIMO-OFDM downlink system. The system-level simulation results show that the proposed scheduler achieves a better balance between optimizing cell throughput and guaranteeing fairness among users than other existing scheduler.

articleTitle: Measurement of Surface EM Field of Planar Circuit in Microwave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A field mapping system used in microwave frequency band is established for the purpose of surface field detection. A section of coaxial line with a protruded inner conductor is used as an electric probe, while a new compact CPW-type loop probe is designed as a magnetic probe. The electric probe used here has a very high sensitivity and could be used up to 18 GHz. The new designed magnetic probe has a very simple structure, compact size of 2.3X2.3 mm and good seIf resonance suppression characteristics, in order to verify the effectiveness of this field mapping system, the EM field distribution of a section of short circuited microstrip line is scanned. By comparing the measurement results with the theoretical ones obtained by 3D simulator (CST MWS), the good performance of the new proposed probes are validated.

articleTitle: Determination of the Melting Layer from Meteorological Radar Data in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A developed algorithm based on the vertical profile of radar reflectivity, has been applied to determine the boundaries of "the melting layer and its thickness. The average values of the melting layer heights are compared with ITU-R recommendations and other obtained results in tropical regions at 500 m resolution range. The results obtained showed lower values for heights of the melting layer.

articleTitle: The Ambiguity Function of MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The ambiguity function of MIMO radar was presented from its own characteristics based on the ambiguity function of bistatic radar. Firstly, right-angle coordinate system was built as reference system for MIMO radar. Secondly, target coordinate and velocity were selected as variables of ambiguity function. Finally, the ambiguity function of MIMO radar was got, which was a combination of the ambiguity function of bistatic radar. The ambiguity function of MIMO radar could directly determine the position of target and velocity and the resolution of the position is higher when more transmitters and receivers were used. The ambiguity function of MIMO radar was unrelated to the reference point.

articleTitle: Simulation investigation of C-Band Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) is a high power microwave (HPM) pulsed device, potentially of gigawatt power, that combines the technologies of magnetically insulated electron flow with a slow-wave structure (SWS)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1~3]</sup>. This combination makes the tube a device capable of operating over a wide voltage range. According to theoretical analysis of the slow-wave structure, a new type C-band MILO has been designed using the advantages of both tapered MILO and load-limited MILO. With the use of a 2.5D fully electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) code, high power microwave is generated from the device with the average output power of 3.4GW, the frequency of 3.5GHz and the power conversion efficiency of 15%, when the applied voltage is 500 kV and current is 45kA.

articleTitle: Blind Adaptive Channel Equalization Based on Affine Projection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this Letter, we address a novel constant modulus algorithm (CMA) based on affine projection algorithm (APA) for blind equalization transmission channel of QPSK systems to deal with inter symbol interference (ISI). Our algorithm is more rapidly convergence, tracking properties and slightly improved steady-state equalization performance than the same category algorithms such as LMS-CMA and NLMS-CMA, and computationally more efficient with similar convergence compared with least squares algorithm (LS-CMA). Simulation results are presented to compare our APA-CMA algorithm with the blind NLMS-CMA and LS-CMA schemes.

articleTitle: Simulation of the EMP Coupling to Circuits inside a Shielding Box by a Wire Penetrated with an Aperture
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is used to simulate the electromagnetic pulse (EMP) induced interference current in circuits inside a shielding box by a wire penetrated with an aperture. Results show that penetrative wire can make the induced interference current in circuits increase greatly, the wire's length and incidence angle of the EMP both have significant influence on the interference current. We also proposed a simple method that using a metal ferrule for suppressing the interference current'.

articleTitle: Optimization of UWB Pyramidal Horn Antenna with load
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: For a UWB pyramidal horn antenna with a curved ridge and a fin, the effect of the resistors at the end of the fin on reflection coefficient or return loss is investigated. The results from both simulation and experiment show that it is a very important factor on its performance that these termination resistors well match the impedance at the antenna's end.

articleTitle: Hammerstein-Like Predistortion Techniques for Wideband Wireless Power Amplifier Linearization
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a novel Hammerstein-like predistortion technique is proposed to linearize the wideband wireless power amplifiers. This Hammerstein-like predistortion technique is based on a Hammerstein-like block configuration, including a memoryless strong nonlinear block followed by a dynamic weak nonlinear block. Here the memoryless strong nonlinear block is utilized to account for the static memoryless nonlinear property, and the weak nonlinear block is employed to eliminate the memory effects. The validation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed Hammerstein-like predistortion technique in suppressing the memory effects in comparison to a traditional one.

articleTitle: A 1.5V Low Power CMOS LNA Design
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A 1. 5 V 0.18mum CMOS LNA for GPS applications has been designed with fully differential topology. Under such a low supply voltage, the fully differential LNA has been simulated, it provides a series of good results in Noise figure, Linearity and Power consumption. The LNA achieves a Noise figure of 1. 5 dB, voltage gain of 32 dB, Power dissipation of 6 mW, and the input reflection coefficient (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>) is -23 dB.

articleTitle: Adaptive Digital Predistorter for Radio Frequency Power Amplifier Linearization
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Power amplifiers (PAs) are inherently nonlinear devices and are used in almost all communications systems. Adaptive digital predistortion is a highly cost-effective way to linearize PAs, and can be implemented by using several ways, which include rational function. This paper presents a rational function based adaptive digital predistorter (RF-ADP) for PA linearization based on the indirect learning architecture. The RF-ADP models amplitude nonlinearity and phase nonlinearity of the predistorter with rational functions. After systematic analysis on the proposed RF-ADP, a low computation complexity adaptive algorithm using least-mean-square is deduced to update coefficient vectors for the inverse amplitude response and forward phase response from the amplitude and phase response at the PA output, respectively. Finally, several computer simulations are done to evaluate the performance of the proposed RF-ADP, and the results show the proposed RF-ADP is very efficient to improve the PA linearity.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach of Automatic Target Recognition using High Resolution Radar Range Profiles
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Generalized information cut (GIC) based on the nonlinear feature mapping using the kernel function is invariant for the linear transformation and the coordinates shift. By comparison and analysis of the angle similarity measurement and generalized information cut, the criterion of generalized information cut is proposed to solve the automatic target recognition using high resolution radar range profile. Feature mapping and inner product is synthesized in the feature space. The range profile data established from four different scaled aircraft models in unclassifiable low dimensional space is mapped into classifiable high dimensional space via the kernel function, and then the linear classifiable pattern transformed from nonlinear unclassifiable pattern is accomplished. Experimental results suggest that the target recognition technique based on the proposed method achieves better anti-noise performance, and is much more efficient in the improvement of recognition ratio of four different aircrafts than using the conventional angle similarity coefficient (the vectorial angle cosine).

articleTitle: Analysis and Study of the Relationship of Energy Consumption and CPU buffer of a wireless sensor node
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to maximize the lifetime of a sensor node, circuits, architecture, algorithms and protocols must be energy efficient. There are many methods to reduce the energy of a node, among them dynamic power manage (DPM) and dynamic voltage supply (DVS) are two effective mechanisms to achieve energy saving. This paper presents the impacts of buffer length and buffer overflow probability on CPU energy. Additional energy savings can be attained by increasing the buffer length without sacrificing performance and reducing an order of magnitude of buffer overflow probability.

articleTitle: A Modified Liao's Absorbing Boundary Condition for FDTD Simulations in 2-D Cylindrical Coordinates with Rotational Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A modified Liao's absorbing boundary condition (ABC) for finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations in 2-D cylindrical coordinates with rotational A modified Liao's absorbing boundary condition (ABC) for finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations in 2-D cylindrical coordinates with rotational symmetry is presented in this paper. Like the ordinary Liao's ABC that was used in Cartesian coordinates, the modified Liao's ABC is easy to implement even near the corners of a computation grid. Further more, the presented Liao's ABC does not encounter stable problem. A numerical example is given to validate the introduced ABC.symmetry is presented in this paper. Like the ordinary Liao's ABC that was used in Cartesian coordinates, the modified Liao's ABC is easy to implement even near the corners of a computation grid. Further more, the presented Liao's ABC does not encounter stable problem. A numerical example is given to validate the introduced ABC.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Modeling the Electromagnetic Spectrum Management System for the Fleet
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A dynamic distributed ship electromagnetic spectrum management system model based on multi-agent system (MAS) was presented in this article. The proposed system model was comprised of five kinds of agent: data-collector agent, device-operator agent, analyze-expert agent, decision-maker agent and require/command agent. Through the cooperation of agents, the system could solve spectrum apportionment for the formation of ships automatically. A well-organized central-plan with hierarchical management architecture was implemented by grading the agents into flagship and the other ships' decision-maker agents groups. It satisfies the distributed and dynamic requirement of ship formation in combined operation.

articleTitle: A Beamspace-based Pre-FFT Beam-forming Algorithm for OFDM Systems with Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a beamspace-based pre-FFT beam-forming algorithm is proposed for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems with antenna arrays in multi-path fading channels. In the receiver, multiple beams are generated firstly to cover the direction of arrival (DOA) range from 0 to 360 degrees. Then one or more delayed paths with large power are estimated by correlation process and two adjacent beams are selected for each path. Thirdly, those paths are extracted respectively from the two adjacent beams by adaptive algorithm and combined together before pre-FFT process. Computer simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has better performance than conventional MMSE based pre-FFT adaptive beam-forming algorithm, such as sample matrix inversion (SMI), etc, in multi-path fading channels.

articleTitle: The analysis and measurements of spot focusing lens antenna resolution
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The sizes of the focal area focused by spot focusing lens antenna and its landscape orientation spatial resolution are analyzed in virtue of wave theory in the paper. Relations between the characteristic of the spot focusing lens antenna at convergence region and the characteristic of the plane caliber antenna which has the same field distributing at infinite region are obtained. The method of the lens antenna spatial resolution measurement is brought forward. The results accord with the theory calculations.

articleTitle: A Statistical Model of UHF Radio Waves in Empty Straight Coal Mine Laneway
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The UHF has been the suitable frequency band at advantage of less propagation attenuation in coal mine. This paper presents a statistical model in empty straight coal mine laneway at UHF which is vital to exploit efficient modulation technology. Besides, the simulation of the wideband channel is carried out at 900MHz, 1800MHz and 2.4GHz. Moreover, the results of simulation and measurement are compared to show the veracity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Performance of Time-Hopping PPAM UWB Multiple Access Communications Over Indoor Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The performance of time-hopping pulse position amplitude modulation (PPAM) for an ultra-wideband (UWB) communication system over fading channels is investigated based on the multipath fading statistics of UWB indoor wireless systems. Frequency selective fading channel is considered for multiple access environment, which is addressed with Gaussian approximation based on single user mode. Error probability expressions are derived from a signal to noise ratio (SNR) perspective for different fading scenarios. Error probability results are verified by Monte Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: Ultra-wide Band Random-signal RADAR Utilizing Microwave Chaos
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we present a new scheme for the realization of a wide-band random-signal RADAR utilizing wide-band chaotic signal generated from microwave chaotic Colpitts oscillator. System simulations show that such RADAR can still work in an environment with worse signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Transient Response of Single or Coupled Wire Antennas Above Dielectric Half-space
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: New time domain integral equations of single and two identical coupled thin wire antennas located above real ground are presented, which can be converted into a simple form expressed only by vector potential. The influence of the lossy ground is taken into account via Fresnel space-time reflection coefficient, and the equations are solved efficiently by method of moments (MOM) combined with marching on in time (MOT) procedure. Results of instances are compared with data from references and the validation of the numerical solutions is verified.

articleTitle: Analysis of Characteristic Impedance of Asymmetrical Coplanar Waveguide using Multi-resolution Time Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The characteristic impedance of asymmetrical coplanar waveguide (ACPW) was calculated using multi-resolution time domain (MRTD) method which based on Daubechies compactly supported scaling functions. The good agreement between this paper and the conventional FDTD method was obtained. Efficiency of MRTD method was compared with FDTD method. Time and frequency domain results have been presented and explained. The curves of characteristic impedance varying with frequency were drawn from 1GHz to 60GHz. The effect of side strip width on characteristic impedance was analyzed.

articleTitle: BER Performance of Position Code Parallel Combinatory Spread Spectrum System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel Position Code Parallel Combinatory Spread Spectrum (PC/PC/SS) communication system is proposed in this paper. PC/PC/SS system can be designed to have higher data transmission capability, even several times compared to ordinary PC/SS system on Gaussian channel. In the proposed system, modulation of position code is applied to each simultaneously transmitting PN sequences. The symbol error rate and average bit error rate performances are analyzed to evaluate the performance of the proposed systems. Furthermore, PC/PC/SS system has excellent secret property than PC/SS and M-ary/SS systems.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Transient Electromagnetic Fields in Substation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Based on the Method of Moment and Fourier transform, a method for the analysis of transient electromagnetic fields generated by buses, power lines and connection lines of devices while switch operating on substations is presented. The results are compared with those of method of MTL (multi-conductor transmission lines), the difference is small. Finally, using the presented method, a model of a 500 kV substation buses without load is set up, and the wave propagation of currents on the power lines and the electric field intensity are analyzed by this method and FFT. These results will be very useful in the next research.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Novel Two-Layer Artificial Magnetic Conductors
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a novel artificial magnetic conductor which we called it, " 2L-AMC" . The frequency bandwidth and resonance frequency of operation will be changed, if the 2L-AMC is placed normal to plane-wave incidence. All possible combinations of 2L-AMC structures including different thicknesses and permeabilities is considered and simulated with CST Microwave studio 2006 software. The results of simulations comply with the theory which is used for conventional AMCs. This novel structures can be used as same as conventional AMCs in all desired frequencies.

articleTitle: Application of CRLH Transmission Lines in Microstrip Filter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel narrow-band bandpass filter using metamaterials is proposed. The filter is composed of cascaded four metamaterial unit cells. We study the properties of the device theoretically and experimentally. The measured results are presented and compared with the results simulated by a high-frequency structure simulator. It is observed that the measured results are good agreement with the simulated results. The proposed filter has narrow bandwidth, low insertion loss, compact dimensions, easy fabrication, and low cost.

articleTitle: Sphere Decoding for MIMO OFDM with the Aid of HARQ
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a computationally efficient sphere decoding method for MIMO OFDM system with the aid of HARQ. This is a cross layer design scheme which adopt the SNR updating information based on retransmission operation to reduced the search radius of sphere detector, it leads the low complexity of sphere detection. Further more, a modification of sphere decoding is proposed to handle non-rectangular constellations, which is more effective for universal modulation signaling.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient and Low-Latency MAC Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, an energy-efficient and low-latency MAC (L-MAC) protocol for wireless sensor networks is proposed. In the protocol, active period is divided into two parts, i. e. receiving period and sending period, and they are staggered hop by hop. That is, after receiving messages from upper-hop node, each node can transmit them to next-hop node immediately in the subsequent sending period. Therefore, the multi-hop end-to-end latency is greatly reduced. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol achieves lower energy consumption and latency than traditional contention-based protocols.

articleTitle: Footprint Adjustment On SFCW-GPR With Modified Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Antennas footprint is an important parameter for good detection result in ground penetrating radar(GPR) survey. The various condition of soil under which a target is buried may change the footprint of an antenna. An antenna with a capacity to adapt, with different soil condition is therefore needed. This type of antenna is capable of keeping the footprint constant in different soil condition. The footprint of an antenna is related to the antennas dimension. In this paper, Modified dipole array is proposed as an adaptive antenna for GPR. With RF Switch circuit, we choose the element on the antenna that will be fed considering to footprint that will be produced. If coupling between element in the array is significant, the array for GPR application will fail to create its adaptation capability. Resistive loading is used to reduce coupling level between elements in the array.

articleTitle: The Pattern Recognition of Radar Signal by Self-Adapted Wavelet
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Radar signal is unbalanced and usually mixed by noises. Wavelet transform is a power tool for analyzing unbalanced signal and multiresolution is the normal way. Also the choice of the wavelet bases is important. A new method for band limited wavelet construction is developed in the radar signal processing, which automatically locks on the frequency band that energy is concentrated. By the algorithm, an optimal scale function is calculated according to the power spectrum of the learning radar signal, the corresponding wavelet can be calculated by two scale relation. With the scale and wavelet filter, the processing result will be the recognized pattern which is similar with the learning radar signal. The experimental results demonstrate the method is effective. Radar signal can be processed in real time.

articleTitle: Effect of Roll Angle Error on Spaceborne ScanSAR Radiometric Calibration in Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The effect of roll angle error on the range dependent gain correction for spaceborne scanning synthetic aperture radar (ScanSAR) is analyzed in this paper. For the bursts image processing of the Scan SAR, the model of the range dependent gain is developed. The basic precision of the roll angle estimation is present to satisfy the requirement of Scan SAR image radiometric correction, and a theoretical guideline for the design and analysis of spaceborne Scan SAR is provided, as verified by simulations.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis and Experimental Research of Shielding Effectiveness of the Cage Built with Wire-Mesh Reinforcementm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A numerical method is presented for calculating shielding effectiveness of the cage built with wire-mesh reinforcement. The model is based on the field approximation for thin wire in the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Then, the proposed method is used to the analysis of shielding effectiveness (SE) of wire-mesh reinforcement. The FDTD results are in very good agreement with the results from the method of moment (MOM). And then a test is made to research shielding effectiveness of wire-mesh reinforcement. The test results are compared with the results from MOM.

articleTitle: A frequency reconfigurable slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposed a frequency reconfigurable CPW center-fed slot antenna. Four pin-diodes are utilized to switch the length of the slot. By tuning the different pairs of diodes on or off, three resonant frequency bands can be obtained. The simulated and measured results validate this concept. This antenna architecture is interesting for wireless applications because it is easily fabricated and integrated with RF circuitry.

articleTitle: Vehicular GPS Monitor System Based on GPRS Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The new vehicular monitor system is combined with Global Positioning System (GPS) and general packet radio service (GPRS) by researching the GPS navigation technology and the shortcomings of current vehicular GPS monitor system. The design characteristics of vehicular GPS monitor system based on GPRS network are analyzed in the thesis.

articleTitle: Linear Time And Frequency Domain Fractionally Spaced Equalization
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The use of over/sampling at the receiver results in colored noise when the bandwidth of the noise-limiting filter is not sufficiently large. In this paper, we investigate the performance of fractionally spaced time and frequency domain equalizer over frequency selective channels with colored noise samples. It is shown that the performance of fractionally spaced equalizer is significantly improved by exploiting the correlation of noise samples. The effect of tap spacing and length of fractionally spaced time domain equalizer are also analyzed. We show that the sampling rate should be given priority to the length of equalizer before the sampling rate reaches a certain number.

articleTitle: Dispersion Characteristics of a Grating-waveguide for Terahertz Radiation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The linear dispersion equation of a grating-waveguide driven by a two-mixed electron beam for an application in Terahertz (THz) radiation is derived with the help of fluid theory, and the interaction of beam-wave is analyzed by the numerical solutions. We study the growth rate of fundamental mode and the second operation mode, and find that the growth rate is considerably enhanced due to the presence of two-stream instability. The peak growth rate versus voltage ratio is investigated, and the result shows that it can be enhanced by the proper choice of voltage ratio.

articleTitle: Effective CAC Scheme in IEEE 802.11e Wireless LANs
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An effective call admission control (CAC) scheme is proposed to improve the performance of IEEE 802.11e wireless local area networks (LANs), which adaptively performances the decision of accepting or rejecting request of new traffic. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly improves quality of service (QoS) in terms of throughput and delay metrics.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dispersion and Harmonic Suppression in Helix TWTs with Studded Slow-Wave-Structure
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: How to make the helix TWTs with wide bandwidth, higher fundamental wave power output, lower harmonic power output, high efficiency and small size is the aim of TWT researches and developments now. This paper describes the simulation results for TWT with different dielectric loading and the helix pitch change. The results show that dielectric shape and pitch change could make TWT wider bandwidth and reduce harmonic power output.

articleTitle: A 0.35-μm BiCMOS Automatic Gain Control IF Amplifier for Radar Receivers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A monolithic automatic gain control (AGC) IF amplifier for radar receivers is designed in AMS 0.35-μm SiGe BiCMOS process. The core circuit of this design is an AGC loop. According to the simulation results, this amplifier is able to process an input IF signal with a dynamic range of 40 dB and its output amplitude keeps a fixed value of 1.5V. It provides a voltage gain up to 60 dB. This AGC amplifier works well over a frequency range from 175 MHz to 275 MHz with a passband ripple of less than 0.5 dB. This circuit consumes less than 100 mW at a single 5-V supply and the layout takes 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Architecture of Planar Phased Array by Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An architecture optimizing method in planar phased array is given based on genetic algorithm (GA). Pattern sidelobe is improved by optimizing array architecture via division of subarrays. Analyze subarray pattern and give out the flow chart of subarray segmentation. By adaptive crossover operator and independent genetic operation, traditional GA is improved. Convergence speed is accelerated and calculation efficiency is enhanced remarkably. Simulations of segmenting 24times28 array into 50 subarrays are provided. Pattern sidelobe is improved by 14.22 dB after 60 generations of GA.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Mutual Coupling on Degree of Freedom of MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The effective channel matrix for a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system is formulated and investigated when mutual coupling among the antenna elements is taken into consideration. It is found that, in general, the antenna mutual coupling decreases the degree of freedom (DoF) of MIMO channels when the inter-element distance is less than several wavelengths. But the DoF reduction is not monotonia with the decreasing of the inter-element distance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Passive Intermodulation Interference in GSM Mobile Communication Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Passive intermodulation (PIM for short) problem in mobile communication is discussed. The PIM property of mobile communication antenna is analyzed by simplified power series method. PIM measurement on GMS mobile communication antenna is done to verify the nonlinear model. Comparison between experimental results and predicted one shows that the used theory is right and practical.

articleTitle: Harmonic-suppressed Elliptic-Function Low-pass Filter Using Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a new microstrip elliptic-function low-pass filter(LPF) using a defected ground structure(DGS) is proposed. By integrating DGS units, the proposed filter provides attenuation- pole for the widc-stopband characteristic due to the resonance characteristic of DGS. The equivalent-circuit model and the 3-D model simulation for the DGS are used to determine the dimension parameters. Etching the designed DGS on the backside of an interdigital elliptic-function LPF, a new microstrip LPF with broad stopband is obtained after- impedance matching. The experimental results show the new filter can suppress the harmonic signal very well.

articleTitle: A Conjugate Gradient FFT Method for Wire Structure
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of the computation of complex wire structure, combined with moment method (MoM), a conjugate gradient FFT method (CG-FFT) is developed to solve the integral equation. Compared with the results computed by NEC, the validity of this method is verified. Using this method, the shielding effectiveness (SE) of wire structure is computed and the factors affect the SE are analyzed.

articleTitle: Interaction between mixture burning plasma and electromagnetic wave in the atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Direct integration method (DI) of FDTD is used to study the scattering characteristic of three dimensional plasma-cloaked targets. By simulating the interaction between mixture burning plasma and electromagnetic wave, the effects of plasma parameters on the radar cross section (RCS) are analyzed. The results indicate that plasma cloaking can greatly reduce RCS of three dimensional plasma-cloaked targets. According to the needs of a new experiment in which chemical mixture is used to generate plasma, DI method is also used to research the RCS of a plasma-cloaked slab. Finally, the numerical result is compared with the experimental result.

articleTitle: A FDTD Method of Quasi-stationary Transient Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: We describe a FDTD method for the quasi-stationary electromagnetic field. An artificial displacement current term is introduced to the Maxwell' s equation, and the FDTD method is applied to the computational area. Then the source is joined as initial conditions and boundary in the air is dealt with under the quasi-stationary situations. The result of numerical calculation indicates that when a coefficient a is between 0.1 and 0.2 in the time step formula, the agreement between the analytical and numerical solutions seems to be basic satisfactory. So this shows the FDTD method is valid to the quasi-stationary electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: Auto Power Control Circuit for Laser Diode Driver
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An auto laser power control (APC) circuit for optical communication laser diode driver (LDD) is proposed. The APC compensates the fluctuation of (laser diode) LD laser power, maintains the output power at the programmed level. The programmed power level can be set by a resistance outside the chip. The design fabricated in 0.25-mum 1P3M CMOS process. HSPICE simulation shows that the floating region of output laser power is within 0.309% with enabled APC, while the temperature is from -20degC to 70degC. Measured results denote perfect linearity of APC character.

articleTitle: Stationary Phase Analysis of a Printed Circular Wire Loop Antenna with Dielectric Superstrate Cover Based on an Efficient Moment Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A circular loop antenna printed on grounded dielectric substrate with another layer of superstrate was analysed in this paper. The research focused on the effects of the superstrate layer on the far field components of the antenna. The far zone characteristics were derived using stationary phase method. Computation of the far field region incorporates the current distribution of the antenna solved by a numerical technique known as Moment Method by applying the curved piecewise sinusoidal functions for both the expansion and the testing functions. Thin wire approximation was applied throughout the research. The radiation efficiency and z-directed power gain were computed as a function of superstrate thickness for various loop resonances.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of Diversity Wire Antenna with Highly-Isolated Ports
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The theory of characteristic modes used in antenna analysis and design is usually more elegant than simple design formulas or purely numerical techniques. The predominant two characteristic currents and the corresponding characteristic patterns of a diversity wire antenna with two highly-isolated ports are given in this paper. The antenna's pattern and the current on it can be approximated by the combination of the characteristic modes 1 and 2.

articleTitle: Study on the Scattering Property of the Impedance Terminated Dipole Array with Finite Reflector by FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The scattering characteristics of the planar array composed of impedance terminated dipoles and a finite reflector are studied by finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. The current distribution on the dipoles and the radar cross section (RCS) of the array are calculated and analyzed. It is seen that the array with resistor terminated dipole tends to give lower RCS.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Analyze UWB Signal Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel method to analyze UWB signal is presented in this paper, namely amplitude probability frequency distribution (APFD). Unlike FT and APD methods that only depict some characteristics of UWB signal in a certain domain, the APFD method proposed in this paper can portray the characteristics of UWB signal from three dimensions space. Neither like STFT method that only observes how the PSD varies with time, this method in this paper can analyze PSD statistical property of UWB signal in long time duration.

articleTitle: Study on the Time Domain Circuit Finite Difference Method and Its Application to Non-Uniform Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the time domain circuit finite difference method is studied. This method can be used to analyze the transient transmission characteristics of the equivalent circuit constructed by the distributed circuit parameters, which are extracted from the non-uniform transmission lines. The stability of the method is studied. The method is then used to analyze the reflected and transmitted pulse waveforms of the equivalent circuit. By comparing the waveforms obtained by this method with those obtained by FDTD, the applicability of this method can be studied.

Author Keywords: time domain circuit finite difference method

articleTitle: The Scheme and Key Components Design of W-band Coherent Doppler Velocity Radar Front-end
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a scheme of W-band coherent Doppler velocity radar front-end, which can be used to measure the velocity of target ranging from 10m/s to 2000m/s. After the comparison of the advantage and disadvantage of several schemes, the scheme using the phase-locked dielectric resonator oscillator (PLDRO) and direct digital synthesis (DDS) is chosen. The two coherent X-band signals are produced by mixer and power-divider mechanism of the PLDRO and DDS. Then, transmitting signal and receiver LO is obtained by the 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order multiplier from the two X-band signals. The superheterodyne receiver is adopted to increase the system signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The finished key components have good performance, indicating that the scheme increases the sensitivity and the resolution of the radar.

articleTitle: Blind 2D-DOA Estimation for Uniform Circular Array
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel blind 2D-DOA estimation method in the uniform circular array based on parallel factor analysis is presented in this paper. Oversampled signal of array antennas is processed by fast Fourier transform, and shows that the Fourier transformed signal has trilinear model characteristics. Parallel factor analysis-based DOA estimation algorithm for the uniform circular array is proposed. This algorithm uses the trilinear decomposition to estimate the direction matrix, and employs the direction matrix characteristics and least squares principle to estimate the DOAs. The simulation results reveal that this algorithm has the better DOA estimation performance, and it works well in the small sampling.

articleTitle: Transient Simulation of Lossy and Nonuniform Multi-Conductor Transmission Lines by Time Domain Finite Element
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new method - time domain finite element (TDFF) - for the transient simulation of lossy and nonuniform multi-conductor transmission lines (MTL) is presented. The method is based on the integral transformation of the telegrapher's equations, combined with recursive convolution method to get the discrete time and space model for frequency-dependent transmission lines. No special technique is required to ensure the stability of the method as in the case of frequency domain moment-matching methods. At last, several numerical experiments show that TDFE-based modeling leads to high accuracy as well as high efficiency.

articleTitle: A W-Band 2nd Subharmonic Injection-Locked Phase-Locked Loop with Large Locking Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a simple approach to obtain the equivalent locking range of the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> subharmonic injection-locked phase locked loop (S-ELPLL). Furthermore, the phase noise of the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> S-ILPLL is analyzed by using a linear phase noise model. Finally, a W-band 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> S-ILPLL circuit was designed and tested; the experimental results demonstrate that the locking range is 60 times larger than that of the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> subharmonic injection-locked oscillator (S- ILO) . On the other hand, the phase noise will not deteriorate in the entire locking range as compared with that of the S-ILO. Therefore, it can be used in novel millimeter wave frequency synthesizer.

articleTitle: A Solution of Time Domain Integral Equation using Hermite Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: For the time-domain integral equation (TDIE) solution, the Marching-on-in time (MOT) algorithm is often employed to calculate the electromagnetic scattering. However, the main drawback of this MOT algorithm is the late-time instability. A method using Laguerre polynomials to obtain stable responses with the electric-field integral equation (EFIE) is presented. In this paper, Hermite Polynomials is used as the temporal basis functions. Numerical results involving currents and coefficients of each order computed by MOO and this method are presented and compared.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Zolotarev Patterns
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Using a modified Chebyshev pattern function with some control parameters, the Zolotarey difference patterns are synthesized by two proposed approaches. One approach consists in forming the pattern function expressed as the multiplication of the modified Chebyshev polynomial with an arctangent function; the other applies an interpolation technique to control the side lobe levels. The control parameters are , given in the expressions of the SLL (Sidelobe Level) and array element number. Under the Fourier relation, the sampling theorem and the FFT algorithm are used to obtain the Zolotarey difference patterns with equal or unequal sidelobe levels. The synthesis examples show the simplicity of these two techniques and the capability to control the pattern' s sidelobe levels.

articleTitle: A Practical Bit and Power Allocation Algorithm for MIMO-OFDM System in Time Varying Wireless Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we propose a computationally efficient bit allocation algorithm for adaptive modulation in MIMO-OFDM systems. In adaptive modulation, QAMs are often employed. However, square QAMs are more power efficient than rectangular QAMs. Based on this fact and the characteristic of MIMO-OFDM channels, the algorithm is developed. The complexity of the proposed algorithm is very low and nearly independent to the total transmission rate. This is applauded especially by systems operate with a high signal-lo-noise ratio (SNR). Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm only requires almost the same power as the optimal Hughes-Hartogs algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis on UWB Ambipolar Multi-pulse Position Modulation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A new UWB (ultra-wideband) modulation scheme called L-ary UWB-TH-AMPPM (Time hopping Ambipolar multi-pulse position modulation) was proposed to get a better UWB communication performance, and the ECWC (extending constant weight code) was introduced to construct the AMPPM signal. The comparison between AMPPM, SPPM (single pulse position modulation) and BPPM (biorthogonal pulse position modulation) was given in four aspects which are data rate, power efficiency, bandwidth efficiency and probability of symbol error respectively. Theory analysis and numerical results show that when the ECWC is chosen rightly, AMPPM can achieve better UWB communication performance than both of the SPPM and BPPM under the same condition.

articleTitle: Accurate Validation Methods for Dynamic Nonlinear Behavioral Models of Wideband RF Power Amplifiers Using Memoryless Predistortion Techniques
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, an accurate validation method for dynamic nonlinear behavioral models of wideband RF high power amplifiers is presented. This method is an indirect validation approach which is based on memoryless predistortion technique to remove the out-of-band spectrum regrowth caused by static memoryless nonlinearities of the power amplifiers. The effectiveness of the model validation method is demonstrated with an L-band push-pull GaAs FET 45-dBm peak-envelope-power amplifier stimulated by a two-carrier 3GPP-FDD WCDMA signal.

articleTitle: Node Selection in Relay-based Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the node selection is investigated in relay-based cellular networks. We propose a novel node selection algorithm, which is designed to maximum the system throughput while consuming the least system bandwidth resources. In the proposed algorithm, mobile station (MS) selects suitable node to access by an optimal model based on the used-bandwidth-ratio. The performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated in a simulation platform based on OPNETTM simulator and compared with that of a simple shortest-distance node selection algorithm. Numerical results show that the proposed algorithm provide a significant throughput gain over the conventional algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive sampling approach based on cubic-spline for fast monostatic RCS calculation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An adaptive sampling method is proposed in this paper to efficiently calculate the scattering from electrically large objects. This cubic-spline-based sampling method is developed by combining Hermite model and spline technique to approximate a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-continous curve through a set of arbitrarily discrete points, which adaptively generated by a coarse-to-fine strategy. Numerical results demonstrate that this method is able to rigorously approximate the result with less computation time when compared to the conventional numerical approximate methods.

articleTitle: Performance of Low Density Parity Check Code Applied in WiBro System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: In Korea, a new broadband wireless access system-High speed Portable Internet (WiBro, Wireless Broadband) is devised to provide high data-rate Internet service. WiBro is considered as the subset of consolidated version of IEEE802. 16c and aims to provide high-speed packet service even when mobile speed comes to 120km/h. This paper presents a brief introduction to the key features of WiBro' s physical layer. Then an advanced channel coding technology- adopted in IEEE802. 16e- structured LDPC is applied to WiBro. The performance of structured LDPC coded WiBro system with different modulation level over AWGN and multi-path channel is simulated. Comparison between structured LDPC and Convolution Turbo Code (CTC) defined in the same proposal are discussed. Simulation results show that the two codes have similar performance when the code rate is low; but LDPC shown better performance than CTC in high code rate, especially at high modulation level.

articleTitle: A Circular Wire Antenna for Ultra Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel circular wire antenna suitable for ultra wideband (UWB) applications is presented in this paper. It consists of a circularly curved wire over a ground plane. The wire structure is designed to deliver approximately the same benefits as a circular disc antenna. Effective length is introduced to analyze the operation of the antenna. Experimental results of the antenna have demonstrated the antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth from 3.1 to 10.6 GHz with a return loss of less than -6 dB. This antenna provides omm-directional radiation patterns consistently over the operating frequencies. Further more, transient response of the antenna is measured to validate the suitability for UWB communication.

articleTitle: On a new method of spectrum sharing in UWB system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Ultra WideBand system (UWB) is characteristic of the wide bandwidth, and it may cause some harmful interference to existing users of the same and nearby bands. So it is impending for us to research on the spectrum management and usage of UWB system aiming at the way it using spectrum as early as possible. In this paper, we are presenting a new method for UWB system to share spectrum with other wireless systems, namely, underlying opportunistic spectrum sharing based on cognitive radio. Its main idea is to smartly and alertly occupy the white frequency bands that aren't fully used by primary users on the condition that the UWB system meets the emission power restriction. The new method helps to improve the flexibility of spectrum sharing and to optimize the spectrum utilization for UWB system.

articleTitle: A Dipole-disk Antenna with Equal Beamwidths
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel method of radiation pattern shaped of dipole-disk antenna by adding a hemisphere conductor is proposed in this paper. The improved dipole-disk antenna has identical beamwidths in E- and H-plane, while its profile does not increase. A model of this antenna is built, stimulated and optimized by a commercial software Ansoft HFSS. Numerical analysis based on stimulation results is made and the design principles involved are described.

articleTitle: Impact of Nanotechnology on Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The next-generation high data rate wireless communication systems are expected to offer a completely new ways to access information and services. The need of higher data transfer rate and bandwidth, along with the requirement for low-cost, high efficiency system implementation, has led to an explosion in new technology development for integrated circuit approaches in RF/microwave area, RF receiver& transmitter, data storage and even power supply. A total solution for high system integration of various components is the trend, the 3D system-on-package concept is considered as one of the future solutions. To realize such as complex concept, nanotechnology could play a significant role for continuing innovation in mobile devices, but it faces a lot challenges. This presentation will touch on the concepts of possible impacts of nanotechnology on communication evolution.

articleTitle: Research on the Harmonics Tester Based on Modern DSP Technology
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a method to design a harmonics tester. The method makes use of modern DSP technology which uses the tool of DSPbuilder of Altera. The design process is to fulfill the FFT computing in MATLAB. Then through being translated and edited, the file is downloaded to FPGA. Finally, the SOPC system is setup by the FPGA, peripheral sampling, keyboard and display circuits. The method can greatly improve the developing efficiency, shorten developing period and reduce costs. The practice has proved the accuracy and validity of the method.

articleTitle: A Dual-Frequency DRA Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with dual-frequency operation based on substrate integrated waveguide is proposed. The proposed antenna has low profile characteristic, just like a microstrip antenna, but has lower dielectric loss and surface wave loss at high frequency. The design approach is discussed, and with the optimization technique, an antenna centered at 19 and 22 GHz is successfully designed, the calculated results show that this antenna has -10dB return loss bandwidth of 400MHz at 19GHz and 420MHz at 22GHz, and the maximum gain of 6dB at 19GHz and 5dB at 22GHz, respectively, the efficiency of this antenna is 89%.

articleTitle: An Efficient Timing and Frequency Synchronization Scheme for OFDM based TETRA Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An efficient timing and frequency synchronization scheme for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based TETRA system is present. TETRA specifies its own preamble for timing synchronization and frequency offset estimation. Two correlators are utilized in this paper to make timing more accurately. A frequency offset estimator with adjustable parameter is proposed in time domain. According to the operation condition, set the proper range of the frequency offset estimator so that the best accuracy can be achieved. Simulation result shows that the proposed schemes exhibit good performances in the channel model defined in TETRA.

articleTitle: Design of a 2.4 GHz low noise amplifier in 0.25 μm CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A RF low noise amplifier used in Wireless Local Area Net system receiver, has been implemented in 0.25 μm CMOS technology. This paper analyzes low-noise amplifier (LNA) cascode topology, noise matching and input matching techniques. Design procedure and simulation results are presented with a 3.3 V supply and 2. 4 GHz frequency, the simulation result of S11 is -14 dB , S21 is 18 dB with 3 dB-BW of 300MHz and NF is about 1.8 dB. The 1 dB compression point is -19 dBm. The chip area is 0. 8 time 0. 6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Dual-Frequency Microstrip Antenna with Wider Beam and Higher Gain at Low-Angle
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A dual-frequency circularly polarized microstrip antenna with wider beams and higher gain at low-angle is proposed in this paper, which is fed by a proximity-coupled microstrip-line. The proposed antenna has no 90-degree hybrid coupler for circular polarization and allows easy connection between a microstrip line and an antenna element. The simulated results verify the circular polarization and show that good return loss and axial ratio characteristics have been obtained.

articleTitle: XML Implementation of Role Based Control in Healthcare Adhoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: As mobile adhoc networks (MANETs) are becoming popular for a variety of applications, so are the issues engulfing corresponding implementations. In this paper, a healthcare application is described for the environment where normal network connectivity may not be available hence adhoc networking of small scale healthcare units and corresponding devices becomes necessary. Different roles of such units are discussed to develop policy framework to facilitate role based access control conformant access. Furthermore, implementation of such access control within a typical healthcare environment is investigated.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Microwave OTH Propagation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The mode of microwave over-the-horizon (OTH) propagation relates to frequency. Many transmission mechanisms are needed to carry on experimental study. In this paper, the transmission characteristics of microwave OTH propagation are analyzed, and some reasons that influence microwave OTH propagation loss are discussed, by marine empirical data. This has guiding sense to the marine OTH communication application.

articleTitle: Integrated Internal GSM850/GSM900/DCS/PCS and Wi-Fi Antennas for Mobile Telephone
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: An internal wideband PIFA antenna and a Wi-Fi antenna are integrated into a mobile telephone. The PIFA antenna works in GSM850/GSM900/DCS/PCS, which assure two kinds of working modes. To assure the performance of two antennas, three Wi-Fi antennas are studied. The proposed antenna is experimentally studied. The three states are also measured under passive and active state to show the effects of the position of Wi-Fi antenna.

articleTitle: Views on Further Improving the Spectrum Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Generally speaking, the article abstractly describes some points of view on further improving of the spectrum efficiency. At first, the author- introduces the current spectrum circumstance and the traditional method of doing this in China. Then the importance of raising the spectrum efficiency and some technical methods are analyzed in the article. The strategy of the spectrum management and the spectrum-sharing technology are also briefly discussed. The needs of the different filed on the frequency spectrum and the trends of development are discussed in the end.

articleTitle: The Simulation and Research on Electromagnetic Character and Coupling Degree of Vehicle Whip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: Antennas have become a frequently used component in modern vehicles. It is very important to research the electromagnetic character of antenna affected by vehicle body and the interference among the antennas. In this paper, a lifelike vehicle model was construct. Then the electromagnetic character of whip antenna at different position on model and the coupling degree between antennas is simulated used CST based FIT technology. The best antenna position was obtained by simulation results at last. The analysis process and simulation results can be ways and means for vehicle electromagnetic compatibility research and vehicle antenna's design.

articleTitle: A universal estimating and measurement method of EMI
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: EMI testing is usually hired professional testing the measuring unit. But this method has some detects, such as the high cost, a long period and do not provide the distributing graph of frequency points and position. Using electromagnetic theory, Neumann formulas and Maxwell equations, a general estimate of the value of EMI testing method is presented in this paper. Oscilloscope, HF magnetic ring induction coil and a small number of testing electrical components and materials are introduced, and then using the interactions between the high frequency magnetic ring induction coil and testing circuit, the EMI is measured indirectly. EMC design can provide sufficient anti-electromagnetic interference measures. It is proved that the method is correct and feasible by the experiments results and the state administration of Radio and TV Detection Center.

articleTitle: Horizontal Dipole Radiation in the Presence of a Lossless Metamaterial Sphere
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: This article discusses the near field properties of the horizontal dipole radiation in the presence of a lossless metamaterial sphere. Based on the approach of Greens function, under different geometrical and electromagnetic parameters, the near field properties are investigated. It could be seen that in the metamaterial sphere, the focusing" phenomenon is observed. It is in consistent with the analysis. Throughout the article, the conventional sphere is utilized as reference. In the conventional material sphere, there are not focuses at all.

articleTitle: A Compact Transition Structure Integrated with DC Feed Filter for Submillimeter Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact transition structure integrated with DC feed low pass filter for submillimeter wave application is designed and simulated. In this structure, the probe transition for suspended microstrip is in longitudinal orientation relative to the waveguide, and a sector suspended microstrip low pass filter is integrated for DC feed circuits. Broad bandwidth with low insert loss (<0.1dB) and high return loss (<-20dB) is achieved by using the commercial simulation software HFSS.

articleTitle: The Bluetooth Body Centre Network Channel Character For Wearable Computer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: The narrow band body centre network based on Bluetooth technology has been constructed by integrated planar inverted-F antenna and the communication channel character has been studied by measurement for wearable computer application. For Bluetooth system, the path loss of different antenna positions on body for measurement can range from -35 dB to -70 dB. If the two antenna located on the arms and moved the two arms, the path loss can change from -40.2 dB to -64.8 dB. The deep breath can affect the path loss within 5 dB and metal ornament such as metal ring can affect about 11.8 dB. The specific absorption rate distribution can also be studied by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method.

articleTitle: A Triple-band Circular Polarization Stacked Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel triple-band circular polarization stacked microstrip antenna is presented. The proposed antenna operates at L band when transmitting left-hand circular polarization signal, and L2 band of GPS and S band when receiving right-hand circular polarization signals. Stacked structure carries out compactness of the antenna and special dual-feed structure has guaranteed good circular polarization performance, what' s more, the extra cone-pedestal greatly enhances gain at low elevation angle.
